Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a VP Finance who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.
Operates with humility, credibility, and sound judgment
Brings a practical, solutions-oriented mindset
Communicates clearly and influences at all levels
A good partner to the program managers – asking what they need before explaining what the number say
Leads with integrity, accountability, and transparency

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will bring experience in social services, healthcare, the boarder public sector, or the not-for-profit sector. Those who understand the operational, funding, and stakeholder dynamics of publicly funded organizations will be particular well positioned for success.
A CPA designation and progressive senior finance leadership experience.
Experience leading finance within a complex, multi-stakeholder organization.
A strong understanding of financial planning, financial reporting, treasury, governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Experience working with Boards and senior executives in a strategic advisory capacity.
The ability to translate financial information into actionable business insights.
A collaborative leadership style and a reputation for building strong relationships across an organization.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President, Finance will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. The organization measures its success not only by financial performance, but by the positive impact it has on the people and communities it serves.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact and help shape the future of a mission-driven organization, we encourage you to apply in confidence.

Thank you for contacting the Government of Nunavut.

Please do not send sensitive or personal information, including (but not limited to): social insurance numbers, birthdates, information of other people, or health information. We will make sure the correct person contacts you if they need more information or if they can answer your question or concern.

This employment opportunity is open to all applicants. Applicants must be currently eligible to work in Canada.

An eligibility list may be created to fill future vacancies.

As this is a term position ending June 2028, current indeterminate Government of Nunavut employees may be offered a competitive transfer assignment for the duration of the term if they are deemed to be the successful candidate, however this is subject to managerial approval.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Corporate Services, the Director, Finance (Director) is the senior financial advisor for the Department of Health. The position is responsible for the financial stewardship and accountability of public funds administered by Health. At the core of their duties is the oversight of the department’s capital and operations and maintenance budget, ensuring that financial resources are allocated efficiently and in accordance with government policies and regulations. The Director of Finance is also accountable for compliance with financial regulations and standards. They must ensure that all financial transactions and operations within the department adhere to the Financial Administrative Manual (FAM) as well as legal and ethical guidelines.

The main responsibilities of the Director are, but are not limited to:

Leading the process of developing the department's annual budget, working with program managers and finance staff to gather input, projections, and cost estimates;
Facilitating the budget approval process, working closely with government agencies, legislative bodies, and stakeholders to address questions, concerns, and revisions;
Overseeing the allocation and execution of budgeted funds, ensuring that expenditures are in line with approved allocations and regulatory guidelines;
Managing the process for budget amendments or revisions as necessary, providing clear justifications and seeking necessary approvals for changes;
Ensuring that all financial reports meet regulatory requirements and government accounting principles, providing transparency and accountability in financial disclosures;
Establishing and maintaining robust internal controls to safeguard financial assets, prevent fraud, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data;
Overseeing and leading a team of financial professionals, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to promote their professional growth and ensure effective departmental operations;
Fostering a culture of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork, working closely with other department heads to ensure financial considerations are integrated into broader strategic planning.

The knowledge, skills, and abilities required for this job are usually obtained through a recognized:

Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, commerce, or related field;
Completion of a professional accounting designation CPA (CMA, CGA or CA);
Eight (8) years of related experience;
Five (5) years of progressive managerial experience in assigning priorities and managing performance of professional teams.

This is a Position of Trust and a satisfactory Criminal Record Check is required.

The Official Languages of Nunavut are Inuktut, English and French. Applicants may submit their resume in any of the official languages of Nunavut. Fluency in more than one of Nunavut’s official languages would be considered an asset. Knowledge of Inuit communities, culture, land, Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, Inuktut and experience working in a northern cross-cultural environment are also considered assets.

Acceptable combinations of education and experience may be considered for this position. We encourage you to apply if you have equivalent years of education and/or experience equal to the education and experience requirements listed above.

The Government of Nunavut is committed to creating a representative workforce; therefore, priority will be given to Nunavut Inuit who self-identify as being enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement in accordance with the Priority Hiring Policy.
Government of Nunavut employees serving a probationary period must obtain and provide written authorization from the deputy head of their employing department. The authorization from the deputy head must accompany your application for your application to be considered.
Possession of a criminal record may not disqualify candidates from being considered. An assessment of the criminal record will be measured against the scope and duties of the position. This is only a requirement for positions that require a satisfactory criminal record or vulnerable sector check.
Applicants may submit their resume in any of the Official Languages of Nunavut.
Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

The onus is on candidates in receipt of foreign post-secondary education credentials to have their foreign credentials assessed through a recognized Canadian education institution. Failure to do so may result in the rejection of their application.

Who We Are

Other.™ is raising the bar in the North American advertising industry, setting a new standard for measurable impact, transparency, and accountability, for both our team and the clients we partner with.

We're a privately owned, Toronto-based team of about 50, led by a small Leadership Team. Our work runs on Propel™, our proprietary operating methodology, and PerformanceLock™, our outcome-linked compensation model, so clients get a system that's been refined across hundreds of engagements rather than a team starting from scratch on every account.

Our growth speaks for itself: we've been named to The Globe & Mail's list of Canada's Top Growing Companies for three consecutive years, and to the Financial Times' The Americas' Fastest Growing Companies 2026 list. This role sits right at the center of what's next: we're bringing Planning and Performance together into one integrated function for the first time, and this hire is who builds it.
Our headquarters is in Toronto's Financial District, steps from Union Station, with a second office steps from Parliament Hill in Ottawa. We operate as a hybrid team, with no in-office mandate.

What You’d Be Up To

As Director of Finance, you’ll play a critical role in shaping the financial health, operational efficiency, and multi-entity growth of the company. You’ll serve as the primary in-house financial anchor, balancing direct oversight of day-to-day operations across our Canadian and US entities with strategic partnership at the executive level, ensuring we’re running with financial precision today and set up to scale cleanly tomorrow.

Lead and manage external fractional partners (Controller and Bookkeeper), establishing clear SLAs, review protocols, and quality control for monthly close cycles.

US Operations, Cross-Border & Intercompany Management

Oversee intercompany accounting, transfer pricing compliance, and intercompany agreements to ensure clean multi-entity consolidation and regulatory alignment.
Coordinate cross-border tax strategy, corporate filings, and state-level compliance (e.g., state sales tax, state income tax, nexus considerations) with specialized external advisors.

Treasury, Cash & Foreign Exchange Management

Own consolidated liquidity visibility across CAD and USD accounts; build and maintain rolling 13-week cash flow models to drive proactive cash planning and inform CFO decision-making.
Operationalize treasury management strategies established by the CFO while ensuring seamless working capital across entities.
Monitor FX risk across multi-currency revenue and expense streams; execute CFO-approved hedging strategies, forward contracts, and intercompany currency transfers to protect against volatility.
Manage day-to-day banking workflows, user access, account administration, and credit line monitoring across Canadian and US financial institutions.

Systems, Process Improvement & Vendor Management

Evaluate, implement and optimize the finance tech stack
Identify and execute automation and system integrations to streamline financial workflows, accelerate month-end closes, and eliminate manual reporting errors across entities.
Manage relationships and service agreements with software providers and external financial vendors in both regions.

Partner directly with the CFO on consolidated budgeting, multi-year forecasting, and strategic capital allocation across business units.
Analyze agency-specific metrics—including client profitability, billable realization rates, and team utilization—to advise leadership on pricing structures and resource planning.

jobs.description:
The Aga Khan Museum connects cultures and communities through the arts. The Museum’s mission is to spark wonder, curiosity, and understanding of Muslim cultures and their connection with other cultures through the arts.

The Toronto-based Museum promotes pluralism through art, storytelling, and enlightened encounters across cultures. Using traditional and contemporary art as well as performing arts as a force for positive change, the Museum’s vision is to impact lives and contribute to more inclusive and peaceful societies. The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

Purpose of Position

Reporting to the Director & Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) responsible for the financial sustainability, stewardship, risk management and financial governance of the organization, while serving as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, Board of Directors, and SLT. The CFO also provides financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.

Leadership Profile

The ideal candidate is a strategic and financially sophisticated executive who combines disciplined stewardship with sound commercial judgment. They are collaborative, analytical and results-oriented, with exceptional integrity, sound judgement and the ability to communicate complex financial matters clearly. They build strong relationships with the internal senior leaders and external partners and are capable of leading through change and complexity while advancing the Museum’s mission.

Ultimately, the CFO is responsible for safeguarding the organization's financial health and long-term sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Serve as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, SLT, and Board of Directors.
Serve as the principal management liaison with the Board, Finance & Audit Committee, and the Investment Committee by preparing and presenting financial information and recommendations, supporting Committee mandates, agendas and decision-making, advising the Board on significant financial risks and ensuring appropriate follow-up on Board and Committee decisions.
Foster collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Build, develop and lead high-performing finance, procurement, and commercial teams with appropriate capabilities, succession, accountability and service orientation.

Financial Stewardship

Develop and maintain a long-term financial sustainability framework, including scenarios focused on funding, operating costs, reserves, liquidity and capital requirements aligned with the organizational strategy of the Museum.
Lead the annual budgeting, multi-year financial planning, forecasting, management reporting and financial performance analysis processes, ensuring that financial resources are aligned with the Museum’s strategic priorities.
Lead the Museum’s preparation for and coordination of the annual external financial statement audit, serving as the senior management liaison with the external auditors and ensuring the timely resolution and communication of significant audit matters, findings and recommendations.
Partner with the Development team to support fundraising and grant objectives through sound financial planning, proposal development and reporting, and ensure appropriate accounting and stewardship of restricted funds, grants, funding agreements and donor-designated resources.
Identify opportunities to enhance revenue, control costs, and improve Museum performance.

Risk, Compliance & Governance

Accountable for the integrity and timeliness of the Museum’s financial statements, management and Board reporting, accounting practices, internal controls, external audit and statutory and regulatory reporting.
Oversee treasury, liquidity, banking and financing arrangements, reserve strategy, investment governance and performance, and the financial planning and oversight of major capital requirements and projects.
Ensures the Museum maintains its tax-exempt charitable status and meets all related tax compliance requirements, including tax reporting, disbursement quotas, and dealings with the CRA.
Lead the Museum’s enterprise risk management framework and consolidated risk reporting, ensuring that significant financial, operational, insurance, legal, contractual, technology and other organizational risks have appropriate ownership, assessment and mitigation plans.
Coordinate the integration of enterprise risk management with business continuity planning and reporting to the Board and relevant Committees.
Provide executive oversight of procurement, ensuring appropriate policies, competitive practices, delegated authorities, contract controls and value for money.

Commercial Activities

Provide financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.
Work with the responsible operational leaders to establish and monitor appropriate revenue, margin and performance targets and ensure effective financial controls and reporting.
Evaluate significant new commercial opportunities for financial viability, organizational capacity, risk and alignment with the Museum’s mission and strategic priorities.
Establish and monitor commercial performance targets.

CPA designation.
MBA or graduate degree in business, finance, or a related field is an asset.
Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience, including at least five years in a senior financial leadership or executive role.
Proven expertise in financial leadership, strategic planning, organizational performance, risk management, and governance.
Experience providing financial and strategic oversight of commercial activities.
Experience presenting to Boards and leading multidisciplinary teams.
Nonprofit and/or charitable sector experience in arts, culture, hospitality, tourism, entertainment, education, or other mission-driven organizations preferred.

Under the leadership of the Vice President, Integrated Management Systems, the Director, Enterprise Solutions – Finance and Operations is responsible for the strategy, evolution, operations, and value creation of the platforms that support Pomerleau’s finance functions and construction operations.

This mandate includes platforms that support accounting, payroll, accounts payable and receivable, procurement, project financial management, and construction operations. It encompasses both the operation and enhancement of current platforms, including CMiC and Procore, as well as the transformation associated with the deployment of the new financial system and the future PMIS.

The Director defines the portfolio roadmap, ensures business continuity throughout the transformation, and prepares the processes, data, integrations, teams, and operating model required to support future platforms.

Working closely with the Finance function and Construction business units, the Director translates business priorities into functional and technology capabilities, ensuring that platforms effectively meet organizational needs.

The Director leads the functional and technical teams, as well as external partners, responsible for platform evolution, integration, operations, and support. They are accountable for platform stability, performance, user adoption, and the value generated for the organization.

jobs.title: Director, Artificial Intelligence, Finance
jobs.description:
Overview

AtkinsRéalis is looking for a Director, Artificial Intelligence, Finance to turn the potential of AI into measurable improvements in how Finance works and how the business makes decisions.

This is a hands-on leadership role. The Director will define a practical AI strategy, identify the opportunities worth pursuing and lead a disciplined portfolio from business case through adoption and verified results. They will also personally design, build, test and help deploy practical Finance agents and AI-enabled workflows within approved enterprise environments.

Success means tangible outcomes: capacity released for higher-value work, faster and better-informed decisions, stronger controls, improved cash performance and protection of project margins. The role is not about deploying technology for its own sake or accumulating pilots that never change how Finance operates.

Leading a small team with a global mandate, the Director will bring together Finance leaders and process owners with the Financial Systems Centre of Excellence (CoE), IT, Global Digital, the Chief Digital Officer's'organization, and data, cybersecurity, privacy and risk specialists. They will develop Finance-specific strategy and governance within enterprise standards, not create competing platforms or policies.

You are a business-led AI and transformation leader who combines strategic ambition, financial discipline and genuine hands-on ability. You can inspire executives, challenge a weak business case and align Finance, Digital, IT and control teams. You are as comfortable discussing strategy as you are building an agent to test an idea with users.

Your role

Set The Strategy And Build Alignment

Define and communicate a value-first AI strategy and roadmap for Global Finance, aligned with Finance priorities, enterprise AI strategy, technology standards and the Financial Systems roadmap.
Determine where AI can materially improve outcomes, where conventional automation or process redesign is preferable, and where an opportunity should not proceed.
Build a shared agenda across FP&A, Controllership, Project Finance and other Finance teams; engage regional and business leaders to identify needs that can scale.
Advise Finance leadership on investment choices, dependencies and risks; secure sponsorship and rally teams that do not report to the Director.

Own a Disciplined Portfolio Of Use Cases

Establish transparent intake and prioritization connected to enterprise channels and governance; assess business value, process and data readiness, feasibility, adoption, total cost and risk.
Maintain a sequenced portfolio with named sponsors, accountable process owners, delivery partners, milestones and clear decisions to proceed, change direction or stop.
Prioritize a few opportunities with a credible path to impact over a large collection of pilots. Candidate areas include reporting commentary, Finance knowledge access, exception handling, forecasting support, collections and project-margin early warning; each requires its own assessment and business case.

Make The Business Case And Prove The Return

Require proportionate business cases before material investment, with baselines, expected benefits, implementation and ongoing costs, risks, dependencies, adoption assumptions and alternatives.
Distinguish time saved from capacity genuinely redeployed and from cost removed; do not treat these as interchangeable financial benefits.
Agree measurement methods and benefit owners before delivery; track investment and realized value at use-case and portfolio levels, with independent validation where appropriate.
Report candidly on adoption, net value, cost and control effectiveness; recommend whether to improve, scale or discontinue initiatives that underperform.

Build, Test And Demonstrate Solutions Personally

Personally design, build and refine selected Finance agents and AI-enabled workflows, especially early prototypes and focused solutions that accelerate learning.
Use Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio hands-on to configure agents, test them with users, assess reliability and improve outputs based on feedback.
Use AI tools regularly in professional work to improve analysis, research, drafting and workflow execution, applying appropriate review and data-handling requirements.
Turn Finance problems into working demonstrations; assess limitations and costs, and decide whether a solution should stop, improve or enter the approved production route.
Stay close enough to delivery to challenge designs, troubleshoot barriers and coach builders, without being the sole developer of enterprise-scale products; partner with Digital and IT on supported deployment.

Establish Practical, Responsible Governance

Translate enterprise AI policy and standards into a Finance operating model covering ownership, intake, risk assessment, testing, approvals, human oversight, monitoring and lifecycle management.
Partner with Digital, IT, the Chief Digital Officer's'organization, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Legal, Risk and Internal Audit to clarify decision rights and navigate the path from idea to approved production use.
Protect sensitive Finance and client information through appropriate access, validation, traceability and human review before AI outputs inform reporting or decisions.
Work with data and process owners on source quality, definitions and controls; reuse approved enterprise platforms and challenge unnecessary complexity without bypassing security or technology accountabilities.

Deliver Through Partnership And Adoption

Partner with the Financial Systems CoE so initiatives fit ERP, EPM and reporting architecture without creating competing technology roadmaps.
Agree delivery responsibilities with Digital and IT while retaining Finance accountability for business outcomes; redesign workflows with process owners around human decisions, exceptions and controls.
Lead communications, training and feedback to build user confidence; create reusable approaches that can scale across regions while respecting genuine process and risk differences.

Lead a Lean, High-impact Team

Build and coach a small team with commercial judgment, hands-on capability and delivery discipline; mobilize a federated network of Finance champions, process owners and enterprise specialists.
Create a culture of curiosity, constructive challenge, accountability and collaboration, including the confidence to recommend "not AI" when appropriate.
Represent Finance in enterprise AI forums and lead by example as both sponsor and practitioner: demonstrate tools, share what works and acknowledge limitations.

About You

A degree in Finance, Business, Technology, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience, is expected.
Significant experience leading AI, data, automation or digital transformation in a complex organization, with demonstrated outcomes beyond proofs of concept.
Experience navigating architecture, cybersecurity, privacy, data governance and risk requirements without losing sight of business value or delivery pace.
Deeper practical experience with Copilot Cowork or Claude Cowork, including a proven record of deploying agentic workflows and demonstrating value in another organization.
Demonstrated hands-on experience building, testing and deploying AI agents, preferably in Microsoft Copilot Studio, with examples you personally created or materially developed.
Experience in an engineering, professional-services or project-based business; familiarity with enterprise Finance platforms, including Oracle-based environments.
Working knowledge of generative AI, agents, analytics and intelligent automation, sufficient to build focused solutions and challenge complex technical designs.
Strong understanding of Finance processes and decisions, ideally including FP&A, reporting, project or contract performance, working capital and financial controls.
Evidence of moving solutions beyond demonstrations to adoption, changed workflows and measurable business outcomes.
Active, capable use of Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT or Claude in day-to-day professional work, with sound judgment about approved tools, sensitive information and human review.
Proven ability to build investment cases, evaluate total cost and alternatives, establish benefit baselines and demonstrate return on investment.
Exceptional collaboration, executive communication and matrix leadership skills; sound judgment about when to scale, simplify or stop.

Rewards & benefits

Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career at AtkinsRéalis in Canada.

Enjoy competitive compensation, employee recognition, and a brilliant range of flexible benefits you can tailor to your health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle needs.

Make the most of diverse opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise.

And take advantage of our hybrid working culture and generous time-off policies to balance a fulfilling career with your personal life.

Be rewarded. Find out more.

About AtkinsRéalis

We're AtkinsRéalis, a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We connect people, data and technology to transform the world's'infrastructure and energy systems. Together, with our industry partners and clients, and our global team of consultants, designers, engineers and project managers, we can change the world. We're committed to leading our clients across our various end markets to engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

Find out more.

Additional information

Analyser et repenser les processus dans les services à la clientèle et les fonctions corporatives, en mobilisant les parties prenantes afin de résoudre les irritants, les lacunes de contrôle, le travail à refaire, les problèmes de données et les besoins non satisfaits avant l’automatisation.

jobs.description:
Director of Clinical Informatics – Enterprise EHR/CIS Implementation

Program:
Symbio – Provincial Clinical Information Solution Program
Client:
Department of Health, Government of New Brunswick (GNB)
Location:
Remote, with travel to New Brunswick at least once per month
Contract Duration:
November 2, 2026 – November 1, 2028, with one optional one-year renewal
Work Schedule:
Full-time
Maximum Rate:
$120 per hour, based on a standard 7.5-hour workday

Position Overview

The Department of Health, Government of New Brunswick, is seeking an experienced Director of Clinical Informatics (BA3)
to support the Symbio Provincial Clinical Information Solution Program. Symbio is a province-wide healthcare transformation initiative focused on replacing fragmented hospital information systems, paper-based clinical records, and disconnected applications with a unified, standardized, and integrated Clinical Information Solution (CIS).
Reporting to the Chief Clinical Information Officer (CCIO) for the Symbio Program and working closely with the CCIO and Chief Nursing Information Officer (CNIO), the successful candidate will establish, mature, and sustain the clinical informatics capabilities, operating methodologies, governance structures, and delivery practices required for the program.
This senior leadership role will oversee the day-to-day delivery of clinical informatics activities across a multi-site acute care health system, ensuring that provincial clinical workflows are standardized while accommodating approved local variations across large, medium, and small hospitals. The Director will bridge clinical stakeholders, physicians, nursing professionals, clinical operations, informatics specialists, and technical EHR/CIS build teams to ensure that the solution reflects approved clinical requirements and supports patient safety, clinical quality, operational readiness, and effective clinician adoption.
The successful candidate will also mentor New Brunswick program personnel, transfer knowledge, and develop sustainable internal capabilities to support the long-term operation and continuous improvement of the provincial clinical information solution.
Key Responsibilities

1. Clinical Informatics Strategy and Program Delivery

Work with the CCIO and CNIO to establish and maintain a sustainable clinical informatics operating model, methodology, and integrated workplan aligned with the Symbio Prepare, Adopt, and Improve journey.

Lead the day-to-day execution of clinical informatics activities across steady-state operations and project-based initiatives.

Establish transparent oversight of milestones, deliverables, progress, risks, dependencies, priorities, and escalations.

Provide regular status and risk reporting to the Department of Health.

Coordinate clinical informatics resources, activities, and priorities to support the program's overall objectives.

2. Provincial Clinical Workflow Standardization and Localization

Develop and lead a methodology for standardizing clinical workflows across a large regional or provincial health system.

Establish consistent clinical workflow standards applicable to large, medium, and small hospital facilities.

Lead the implementation and localization of standardized workflows to accommodate facility-specific operational needs while preserving provincial standards.

Assess proposed local variations, document their rationale, evaluate their impact, and support formal review and approval through established governance processes.

Ensure workflow design promotes consistency, efficiency, patient safety, and effective care delivery across participating facilities.

3. Physician and Clinician Engagement

Develop and execute engagement and advocacy approaches for physician groups, nursing professionals, and other clinical stakeholders.

Engage physician leads and frontline clinicians in clinical workflow design, EHR/CIS configuration decisions, validation, and implementation planning.

Represent physician and clinician needs in clinical governance forums, design discussions, prioritization decisions, and issue resolution.

Facilitate collaboration between clinical stakeholders, program leadership, clinical operations, and technical delivery teams.

Ensure frontline clinical requirements are accurately reflected in approved workflows, system design, and implementation decisions.

4. Clinical Governance and Decision-Making

Establish, lead, or support clinical working groups, committees, and governance forums responsible for clinical workflows, EHR/CIS design, prioritization, and cross-site decisions.

Define decision-making processes, governance structures, escalation pathways, and accountability mechanisms.

Facilitate timely and transparent resolution of clinical design issues, competing priorities, and workflow conflicts.

Maintain documented decisions, approved requirements, priorities, risks, actions, and escalations.

Ensure governance decisions are communicated to relevant clinical, operational, informatics, and technical stakeholders.

5. Clinical Informatics and Technical Build Team Alignment

Manage the day-to-day relationship between clinical informatics and technical EHR/CIS build teams.

Translate clinical requirements, approved workflows, and clinical design decisions into clear functional requirements and build specifications.

Prioritize build requests and coordinate capacity, dependencies, competing requirements, and delivery timelines.

Resolve conflicts between clinical needs, technical constraints, and approved design standards.

Oversee delivery against approved requirements and ensure that system configuration reflects intended clinical workflows.

Establish effective processes for requirement traceability, design review, build validation, and issue resolution.

6. Technical Build Governance and Oversight

Provide leadership and oversight to technical EHR/CIS build teams.

Establish build governance, standardized build methodologies, configuration standards, and delivery processes.

Manage build priorities, resource capacity, work allocation, and competing demands.

Oversee system build, configuration, testing, release management, and deployment readiness.

Coordinate planning and impact assessments for major system changes, including code upgrades and other significant platform changes.

Ensure appropriate alignment between technical delivery, clinical requirements, system quality, and operational needs.

7. Clinical Workflow Validation, Testing, and Release Readiness

Define and lead clinical workflow validation, testing, release-readiness, and cutover approaches.

Coordinate clinical and technical testing cycles to verify that configured workflows meet approved requirements.

Assess system quality, clinical safety, operational readiness, and unresolved risks before deployment.

Establish and apply clear go/no-go criteria and provide release-readiness recommendations.

Develop and oversee clinical and technical cutover plans, including stakeholder coordination, issue escalation, and contingency considerations.

Ensure readiness decisions are supported by documented validation results, identified risks, and appropriate stakeholder approvals.

8. Patient Safety and Clinical Quality

Embed patient safety and clinical quality considerations into EHR/CIS design, configuration, validation, and implementation.

Apply comprehensive clinical informatics knowledge across clinical documentation, order management, order sets, clinical decision support, medication management, and workflow analysis.

Focus on medication systems and orders management to ensure the solution supports safe and reliable clinical practices.

Partner with Clinical Operations to translate intended safety and quality outcomes into practical operational improvements.

Identify clinical workflow risks, system-related safety concerns, and improvement opportunities and coordinate appropriate mitigation activities.

9. Go-Live, Incident Management, and Stabilization

Lead or support planning and execution for large-scale EHR/CIS activations from a clinical informatics perspective.

Coordinate clinical readiness activities, activation planning, command-centre operations, and incident-management processes.

Support clinical incident triage, prioritization, escalation, and resolution during implementation and stabilization.

Monitor clinical workflow performance and system issues following deployment.

Coordinate stabilization activities and transition the program toward sustained operations and continuous optimization.

Ensure clinical stakeholders receive the support required to maintain safe and effective care delivery during system transitions.

10. Clinician Education, Adoption, and Optimization

Develop and support clinician education strategies and learning materials for new and revised clinical workflows.

Apply adult learning principles to training design, delivery, and evaluation.

Coordinate clinician readiness, adoption support, and communication activities.

Evaluate education effectiveness and identify opportunities to strengthen user confidence and system utilization.

Lead post-go-live optimization activities based on clinician feedback, operational performance, workflow issues, and lessons learned.

Support continuous improvement of clinical workflows and system usability.

11. Clinical Informatics Team Leadership and Enterprise EHR/CIS Experience

Build, lead, mentor, and develop clinical informatics teams supporting enterprise-scale EHR/CIS implementation and optimization.

Provide direction, coaching, and oversight to clinical informatics personnel and multidisciplinary delivery teams.

Apply experience with a major enterprise EHR/CIS platform to the platform selected for the Symbio Program.

Establish sustainable team practices, operating procedures, and knowledge-sharing mechanisms.

Promote collaboration across clinical, operational, informatics, and technical teams.

12. Knowledge Transfer and Capability Development

Mentor and develop New Brunswick program personnel throughout the engagement.

Transfer practical knowledge, skills, methodologies, and expertise in clinical workflow standardization, facilitation, governance, validation, and documentation.

Develop and maintain reusable processes, guidance, and documentation that support continuity of clinical informatics operations.

Enable internal program personnel to independently apply established practices and sustain the program beyond the engagement.

Support the long-term maturity and self-sufficiency of the province's clinical informatics capabilities.

jobs.title: Vice President, Portfolio Analytics
jobs.description:
About Citco

JOB DESCRIPTION

The market leader. The premier provider. The best in the business. At Citco, we’ve been the front-runner in our field since our incorporation in 1948 led to the evolution of the asset servicing sector itself. This pioneering spirit continues to guide us today as we innovate and expand, push beyond the boundaries of our industry, and shape its future. From working exclusively with hedge funds to serving all alternatives, corporations and private clients, our organization has grown immensely across asset classes and geographies. For us, this progress is a pattern that we’ll only maintain as we move forward, always prioritizing our performance. So for those who want to play at the top of their game and be at the vanguard of their space, we say: Welcome to Citco.

About The Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

A challenging and exciting role in a rapidly growing industry, Portfolio Analytics services across a diverse client base spanning hedge funds, private markets and multi-asset strategies across North America, the United Kingdom, Continental Europe and Asia. The Vice President of the Portfolio Analytics group will take a senior leadership role managing existing US client relationships, ensuring client retention, and driving sales, marketing and business development initiatives across the region. The team provides ad-hoc and regulatory risk reports that include, but are not limited to, exposure and P&L reports, limits monitoring, scenario analysis, stress testing, value-at-risk and fund performance analytics - supporting clients across a broad range of strategies and structures.

The role provides a unique opportunity to work closely with a wide range of securities, derivatives and structured products in many currencies traded across global markets, and to lead the build-out of a structured, high-performing client service model across the US book. The individual's duties will include, but are not limited to, client onboarding project management, senior client relationship leadership, team management, and the training and development of staff — mirroring and helping to embed a proven operating model already established elsewhere in the group.

Responsibilities

Your Role:

Business Development & Commercial Acumen — Take an active, leading role in the CFS 'new business acquisition' process from a Portfolio Analytics perspective, effectively demonstrating our suite of Portfolio Analytics services to potential clients as well as new or enhanced services to existing clients, positioning this as a core driver of the role; evaluate the viability of current and new business proposals with emphasis on tactical issues and barriers
Client Relationship Management — Own and lead senior client relationships across the US book, participating in regular client calls and working closely with the global Client Integration team who oversee and project manage the firm-wide onboarding process
Reporting of Client KPIs — Own and maintain the KPI and RAG framework across the US client base, supervising junior team members in day-to-day tracking and reporting to support senior management oversight
Team Leadership & Management — Provide day-to-day leadership and management of the US Portfolio Analytics team, embedding a structured, KPI-driven client service model and ensuring consistent standards of client oversight and RAG reporting across the book
Communication — Use appropriate interpersonal styles and techniques to gain acceptance and help others understand the importance of the vision on the day-to-day reality of the risk reporting process
Building Networks - Proactively build strong relationships with Client Service and Business Development colleagues across CFS offices as a first priority, while also networking across departments (Valuation/Profit & Loss, Operations, Internal Audit, Integration, etc.) to establish collaborative business relationships at all levels and facilitate the accomplishment of business objectives
Leading & Managing Others — Embody the CFS culture, lead and inspire team through change, encourage others to seek opportunities for different approaches to address problems and opportunities
Organization & Resource Management — Oversee the US team with responsibility for pre-sales, onboarding, client coverage planning, and other new business initiatives
Building and Retaining Organizational Talent —Focus on identifying, developing, deploying and retaining key talent within the US team (including succession planning) for the future success of CFS, initiating strategies to develop internal talent through ongoing training and conducting timely performance evaluations.
Operational Decision-making — Commit and take responsibility for tactical decisions, adopting innovative approaches to move resolution of challenges to completion; communicate outcomes to all stakeholders and contribute to CFS vision and strategy
Execution — Execute business strategy by aligning communication, accountabilities, skills, internal processes and measurement to ensure sustainable and profitable results
Client Risk & Continuity Oversight — Identify and manage clients with elevated customisation and key person risk, ensuring documented continuity plans are in place and escalating concentration risk where appropriate

Qualifications

About You:

Drive for Results — Possessing an energetic and tenacious achievement orientation; proactively seeking opportunities to drive performance of self and team, and setting stretching goals; managing personal and group strengths and opportunities
Navigating Complexity — Proactively and quickly making sense of complex issues where ambiguity exists; communicating complicated information concisely and logically
Excellent analytical, problem-solving and communication skills, with proven ability to summarise and interpret client requirements
Aspiration to become a subject matter expert in proprietary risk solutions
Someone who enjoys project-based work, collaboration across teams, and dealing directly with clients — no two days the same
Quantitative background with a Bachelor's/higher level degree or professional qualification (MSc, PhD, CQF, FRM, PRMIA, GARP, CFA, FIA)
Proficient in Excel, VBA, SQL, with Python experience in particular advantageous
Knowledge of business intelligence tools such as Qlik Sense (or Tableau) and Jaspersoft is a plus
7–10 years' experience in investment and regulatory risk reporting and performance analytics in funds/asset management/banking/insurance - including hedge fund, private markets and multi-asset strategies , with demonstrated experience in client relationship leadership, team management, pre-sales, onboarding and business development
Prior experience managing or supervising a client-facing team is required
Knowledge of market, credit, liquidity and counterparty risk measurement and management under regulatory frameworks such as Form PF, Form CPO-PQR, Annex IV, Basel III/CRD IV/CRR and Solvency II is advantageous
Candidates must be willing to travel to the United States for business purposes

Salary Range:
$115,000 - 155,000

Our Benefits

Your well-being is of paramount importance and central to our success here at Citco. Job Overview:

The Director, Corporate Development and Strategy leads the strategic planning and development, M&A, and special strategic projects agenda for ETG’s Pulses vertical. Reporting to the Global CEO and working closely with the CFO, the executive leadership team, consultants, and key operating personnel, the Director drives the implementation of the vertical’s long-term growth strategy and provides support to all areas of the business to achieve the company’s strategic objectives. The role combines investment-banking-level transaction rigor with a deep commercial understanding of the pulses value chain to turn strategy into executed, value-creating deals, projects, and initiatives.

Responsibilities:

Corporate Strategy & Planning:

Lead implementation and ongoing development of the Pulses vertical’s multi-year strategic plan, including supporting new project development, M&A, and business analysis.
Identify and evaluate growth avenues—new geographies, adjacent products, value-added processing, and vertical integration.
Support the annual strategic planning cycle with the CEO, CFO, and business leaders, translating strategy into measurable targets and KPIs.
Monitor industry, commodity, trade-policy, and competitive developments and advise leadership on their implications.
Translate complex financial data into actionable insights for Board and investor presentations.
Prepare strategy materials for the Board and executive committee.

M&A and Corporate Transactions:

Own the end-to-end M&A process: target screening, origination, valuation, deal structuring, negotiation, due diligence, and closing.
Build and maintain a prioritized pipeline of acquisition, divestiture, joint venture, and partnership opportunities.
Lead transaction workstreams for carve-outs, acquisitions, and redomiciliation, coordinating finance, tax, legal, and operations.
Develop investment cases and present recommendations to the CEO, executive committee, and Board.
Oversee post-acquisition integration planning and track realization of synergies against the investment case.

Investor/Stakeholder Relations:

Shape and own the vertical’s equity story, ensuring coherent messaging across strategy, structure, valuation, and growth.
Lead preparation of investor materials—CIMs, management presentations, Q&A briefs, and valuation summaries—and support the CEO and CFO in investor engagements.
Direct due diligence and data room readiness for capital raises and investor processes.
Evaluate capital structure, refinancing, and funding alternatives in support of strategic priorities.
Benchmark peer performance, transaction multiples, and sector valuations to inform positioning.
Support Finance in raising debt and equity funding to support business growth.

Special Strategic Projects:

Lead special strategic projects at the direction of the CEO, from scoping and analysis through recommendation and implementation.
Conduct business analysis of operations, product lines, facilities, and markets to inform decisions on whether to invest, grow, restructure, or exit.
Lead portfolio and asset rationalization reviews, including consolidation of facilities, product lines, and legal entities, and divestiture of non-core assets.
Design and support internal reorganizations, including changes to organizational structure, reporting lines, and operating models.
Build business cases that quantify financial, operational, and people impacts, and track realization of expected benefits after implementation.
Coordinate cross-functional project teams and external consultants to deliver projects on time and on budget.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management:

Build and lead a high-performing corporate development and strategy function within the company, earning credibility across the organization by consistently adding value.
Manage relationships with investment banks, advisors, valuation firms, legal firms, private equity investors, and prospective partners.
Partner with operations, finance, legal, and IT leaders to align strategic initiatives with execution.
Serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO and executive leadership on strategic and transaction matters.

Employment Qualifications & Requirements:

MBA, CFA, and/or Chartered Accountant (CA/CPA) designation preferred.
10+ years of experience in corporate development, M&A, investment banking, private equity, or strategy consulting, including at least 3 years in a leadership role.
Proven track record of originating, leading, and closing multiple M&A transactions end to end, and of leading complex cross-functional initiatives such as reorganizations and business rationalizations.
Experience in agribusiness, commodities, food, or manufacturing sectors in global environments strongly preferred.
Deep expertise in valuation, financial modeling, deal structuring, and negotiation.
Experience preparing Board-level strategy materials and engaging directly with investors, lenders, and advisors.
Strong grounding in IFRS, multi-entity structures, and cross-border transactions.
Comfortable with frequent international and domestic travel.

Personal Attributes:

Strategic thinker with strong commercial judgment and a bias for execution.
Credible, influential presence with Boards, executives, investors, and counterparties.
Skilled negotiator who manages ambiguity, confidentiality, and competing priorities with discretion.
Exceptional communicator—able to craft clear narratives for financial and non-financial audiences.
Hands-on change leader who builds buy-in across the organization and delivers under tight timelines.

Success in this Role Means:

Maintaining organizational focus on a Board-endorsed growth strategy for the Pulses vertical with a well-prioritized execution roadmap.
A robust deal pipeline, closed transactions, and special strategic projects that deliver on their investment cases and targeted benefits.
A company story that strengthens investor and lender confidence in the vertical’s performance and growth.
A high-caliber corporate development and strategy function trusted by leadership.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
Join a Challenger

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.

What's kept us moving?
The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.

We can’t wait to get to know you!

The Work

The Senior Director, Financial Planning and Analysis leads the Bank’s enterprise financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, and management reporting activities and oversees the Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence within the VP, Financial Planning & Analysis portfolio. The role establishes an integrated view of financial performance, outlook, risks, and opportunities to support executive decision-making and disciplined resource and capital allocation.

The role partners with business and functional leaders to translate strategic priorities into financial plans, challenge assumptions, assess performance drivers, and provide timely, decision-useful insight. It is accountable for the quality, consistency, governance, and continuous improvement of planning and forecasting processes and for establishing a high-performing Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence that scales common standards, tools, models, data, and insight across the Bank.

Financial Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Lead the annual budget, periodic forecast, and multi-year financial planning processes, integrating business plans, economic assumptions, balance sheet and income statement drivers, and enterprise priorities.
Establish planning calendars, standards, controls, accountabilities, and review forums that support complete, accurate, timely, and comparable submissions across the Bank.
Provide an integrated view of actual and forecast performance, including revenue, net interest margin, expenses, profitability, return on equity, capital implications, and key non-financial drivers.
Lead scenario and sensitivity analysis to assess the financial implications of changing market conditions, strategic choices, investments, and emerging risks.
Identify material variances, trends, and forecast risks; ensure clear ownership of actions and provide concise recommendations to senior leadership.

Capital Forecasting, Strategic Capital Allocation, ICAAP & Stress Testing

Lead enterprise capital forecasting and provide a forward-looking view of regulatory capital, leverage, capital generation, and deployment under the strategic and financial plan.
Assess capital capacity, requirements, and trade-offs to support the allocation of capital to strategic investments, business growth, acquisitions, and other enterprise priorities.
Partner with Treasury, Risk Management, business leaders, and other Finance teams to align capital forecasts with earnings, balance sheet growth, risk-weighted assets, funding plans, internal capital targets, and management buffers.
Lead the consolidation of financial forecasts and capital impacts for the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process, enterprise-wide stress testing, regulatory stress testing, and related scenario analysis.
Evaluate adverse but plausible scenarios, key sensitivities, and management actions; identify potential capital constraints or vulnerabilities and recommend actions to protect resilience and support strategic objectives.
Establish robust governance, controls, documentation, and executive reporting for capital assumptions, methodologies, forecasts, stress-testing outputs, and capital-allocation decisions.

Executive & Strategic Financial Storytelling

Lead the development and presentation of clear, Board-ready financial narratives that explain enterprise performance, outlook, key drivers, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Translate complex financial, operational, and strategic analysis into concise, decision-oriented messages tailored to the Board, executive leadership, and management governance forums.
Provide strategic oversight of consolidated financial results and outlook, ensuring consistency across the income statement, balance sheet, capital, business segments, and key performance indicators.
Connect actual and forecast performance to the Bank’s strategy, external environment, and value-creation priorities, highlighting the implications of trends, trade-offs, and emerging issues.
Establish executive communication standards that are punchline-first, analytically sound, and supported by clear evidence, sensitivities, and actionable recommendations.
Coordinate across Finance, Treasury, Strategy, Investor Relations, Risk Management, and business finance partners to maintain a consistent enterprise financial story across Board, executive, regulatory, and external materials.

Management Reporting, Data & Insight

Oversee recurring management reporting and dashboards, ensuring that measures, definitions, commentary, and source data are consistent and decision-useful.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial drivers that connect strategic objectives, operating activity, and financial outcomes.
Strengthen data quality, model governance, documentation, controls, and review practices for material planning and management reporting outputs.
Drive automation and simplification of planning, forecasting, modelling, and reporting processes to improve speed, accuracy, transparency, and analytical capacity.
Partner with Data and Technology stakeholders on requirements, prioritization, testing, implementation, and adoption of financial planning and analytics capabilities.

Leadership, Governance & Continuous Improvement

Establish and oversee the Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence, including its mandate, governance, operating model, service catalogue, priorities, measures, and capability roadmap.
Develop common planning, forecasting, modelling, reporting, and business-partnering standards, and support adoption across Financial Planning & Analysis and partner teams.
Build reusable tools, templates, driver libraries, scenario models, data definitions, and analytical practices that improve consistency, speed, and decision usefulness.
Create a community of practice that strengthens capability through coaching, knowledge sharing, quality review, and continuous learning.
Lead, coach, and develop a team of finance professionals; establish clear accountability, effective succession and development practices, and high standards for analysis and communication.
Maintain an effective control environment for planning, forecasting, modelling, and management reporting, and address issues identified through review, audit, or control testing.

Lets Talk About You!

University degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
CPA or CFA designation or an equivalent recognized finance designation.
At least 12 years of progressive finance experience, including substantial experience in financial planning and analysis, forecasting, management reporting, financial modelling, and executive decision support.
Senior leadership and people-management experience, including experience setting functional priorities, reviewing complex work, coaching leaders and professionals, and delivering through others.
Advanced knowledge of financial statements, performance drivers, budgeting, forecasting, scenario analysis, profitability, return on equity, and capital-aware decision-making within financial services.
Experience producing and presenting concise analysis for executives and governance forums, with the judgment to distinguish material issues, challenge assumptions, and recommend action.
Advanced spreadsheet and presentation skills and experience with enterprise planning, reporting, business intelligence, and financial data tools. Specific systems: To be confirmed.
Strong written and verbal communication, stakeholder-management, analytical, problem-solving, organization, and change-leadership skills.
Experience in a Canadian bank or other regulated financial institution, including knowledge of banking products, net interest margin, balance sheet drivers, capital, and regulatory considerations.

What we offer [For full-time permanent roles]

💰 Competitive discretionary bonus

✨ Market leading RRSP match program

🩺 Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits

📝 Employee Share Purchase Plan

👶🏽 Maternity/Parental top-up while you care for your little one

🏝 Generous vacation policy and personal days

🖥 Virtual events to connect with your fellow colleagues

🎓 Professional development and comprehensive Career Development program

💛 A fulfilling opportunity to join one of the top FinTechs and help create a new kind of banking experience

.

Equity, Diversity & Inclusion

EQ is committed to building an inclusive, accessible environment where every employee feels valued, respected, and supported. About Hatfield

Hatfield, a proudly Canadian company, has been serving our clients and our community for over 50 years. We have been recognized as one of Canada’s Top SME Employers in 2025. When you join Hatfield, you choose a career that makes a difference in the lives of all those who share our planet.

Hatfield is seeking a Leader of Finance. This position will provide oversight of financial planning, management of financial risks, record-keeping, and financial reporting. The Leader of Finance will work closely with and is accountable to Hatfield’s Managing Partners and Board, reporting directly to the Senior Vice President & Managing Partner.

Responsibilities

Financial Operations:

Cash flow forecasting and monitoring cash flow to ensure the company has sufficient liquidity for operations and investments.
Leading financial forecasting, budgeting, and long-term planning.
Overseeing tax compliance and optimization strategies in collaboration with external advisors.
Ensuring the company’s financial systems are legally compliant and progressively support operations and future growth.
Overseeing the company’s annual operating budget to ensure that financial resources are used efficiently and effectively.
Collaborating with operations to optimize cost-effective sourcing, improve equipment tracking, and streamline charge-out processes to enhance operational efficiency.

Financial Oversight and Reporting:

Overseeing the company’s financial operations and ensuring timely and accurate financial reports and practices.
Ensuring that financial reports are compliant with Canadian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles and accurately represent the company’s financial position.
Maintaining effective internal controls and financial review processes to ensure the accuracy and reliability of financial statements.

Strategic Initiatives

Supporting company goals and objectives with progressive financial strategies.
Collaborating with other senior managers to make informed decisions about investments, capital structure, and profitability.

Leadership:

Building and leading an effective finance and accounting team ensuring they are motivated and performing to the best of their abilities.
Leading the Hatfield Finance Committee and ensuring the Committee’s efforts support Hatfield’s financial objectives.
Overseeing financial planning and analysis functions to support strategic decision-making and business growth.

Risk Management:

Managing insurance policy renewals, ensuring adequate coverage, and addressing compliance with regulatory requirements.
Identifying and addressing financial risks to the company and recommending measures to mitigate them.

Mergers and Acquisitions:

Providing financial analysis and recommendations on potential M&A opportunities.
Evaluating financial viability and risks factors associated with potential acquisitions.

Board Consultation:

Advising the Hatfield Board and the Managing Partners on corporate financial strategies.

Strong knowledge of accounting principles and a background with data analysis.

Strong working knowledge of Power BI, including using, interpreting, and presenting financial dashboards. Experience designing dashboards is an asset.

Experience without limits—in your work, your growth, and your impact.

The Opportunity

We're looking for a commercially minded and operationally focused Finance Director, Fabrication Operations
to serve as the finance lead and strategic business partner for our North American fabrication network.

Partnering directly with the Head of Fabrication, you will help build the financial and operational foundation for a growing multi-site production organization. This role is ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance and operations, can connect financial performance to what is happening on the production floor, and enjoys transforming data into actionable business decisions.

You will play a critical role in improving profitability, building reporting and forecasting capabilities, optimizing capacity utilization, and supporting the integration and standardization of fabrication operations across the network.

What You'll Do

Financial Performance & Cost Management

Build and maintain consistent individual and consolidated P&Ls across four fabrication facilities, along with separate P&Ls for storage, rental inventory, and fleet operations.
Conduct a comprehensive assessment of facility cost structures, labor models, capacity utilization, and current reporting practices.
Develop budgeting, forecasting, and scenario-planning models covering labor, overtime, freelance resources, subcontracting, storage, fleet, and facility expenses.
Establish project profitability reviews to compare estimated versus actual margins and create feedback loops that improve future estimating and pricing decisions.
Analyze labor productivity, utilization, overhead absorption, and operational drivers of profitability.
Partner with operational leaders to identify opportunities to improve margins, reduce waste, optimize labor deployment, and increase financial discipline.
Lead monthly performance reviews with fabrication leadership teams.

Capacity Planning & Network Optimization

Map capacity against demand across the fabrication network and develop reporting that supports more effective planning and resource allocation.
Improve pipeline visibility to provide a reliable view of future fabrication demand and workload requirements.
Separate fabrication, non-fabrication, and insourced work streams to support accurate capacity planning and decision-making.
Support long-term network planning, including facility footprint decisions, capability investments, and capital expenditure evaluations.
Build financial models that support insource versus outsource decisions, staffing strategies, overtime management, and facility investments.
Support vendor consolidation initiatives, rebate tracking, and procurement savings opportunities.

Reporting, KPIs & Integration

Develop and implement a standardized KPI framework across all fabrication locations, including utilization, throughput, overtime, on-time delivery, rework, and profitability metrics.
Launch and maintain executive dashboards covering network performance, financial performance, pipeline, capacity utilization, storage, rental inventory, and fleet operations.
Establish standardized reporting and performance management processes across all locations.
Support the integration of Jack Morton and Impact XM fabrication operations through common definitions, metrics, and processes for job costing, work orders, change orders, and markup structures.
Support D365 adoption and help reduce reliance on manual processes and offline workarounds.
Partner across Fabrication, Finance, Commercial, Estimating, Creative, Account, and Project Management teams to improve planning, visibility, profitability, and operational execution.

What We're Looking For

8-12+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant experience supporting manufacturing, fabrication, production, logistics, or other operational environments.
Strong understanding of cost accounting, job costing, labor utilization, overhead allocation, margin analysis, and operational performance management.
Experience supporting multiple facilities, locations, or operating units.
Demonstrated ability to build financial models, forecasting processes, dashboards, and KPI frameworks from the ground up.
Experience driving finance process improvements, operational standardization, and systems adoption within growing or transforming organizations.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex financial information into actionable operational recommendations.
Experience evaluating capital investments and developing ROI-based business cases.
Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence leaders across functions.
Comfortable working in fast-paced, project-based environments where priorities can shift quickly.
Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills; experience with ERP systems and business intelligence tools preferred.
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. CPA, CMA, or MBA is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first six months, you will have:

Assessed the financial and operational performance of all fabrication facilities and support operations.
Established consistent facility, storage, rental, and fleet P&Ls.
Implemented a standardized KPI and reporting framework across the network.
Launched fabrication performance dashboards that provide clear visibility into profitability, utilization, capacity, and demand.
Built forecasting and scenario-planning tools that support operational decision-making.
Established a regular performance review cadence with facility leaders.
Improved visibility into project profitability and manufacturing economics.
Helped advance the integration and standardization of production operations across Jack Morton.

Success in this role means creating financial visibility where it does not exist today, improving profitability and operational performance, establishing disciplined forecasting and reporting processes, and helping build a scalable fabrication organization capable of supporting future growth.

jobs.description:
About Gambler First Nation

Gambler First Nation (GFN) is an Ojibway First Nation located near Binscarth in southwestern Manitoba, within Treaty 4 territory. The Nation’s primary reserve, Gambler 63, is situated in a rural setting along the Assiniboine Valley, offering a close‑knit community environment rooted in strong cultural traditions and a deep connection to the land. GFN is one of the smaller First Nations in Manitoba, with a total registered membership of approximately 330 members, the majority of whom live off‑reserve. Despite its size, the Nation maintains an active governance structure and delivers a range of programs and services to support the wellbeing of its members, both on‑ and off‑reserve.

The Nation is a member of the West Region Tribal Council and works collaboratively with regional partners and other First Nations to advance shared priorities and access collective services. Gambler First Nation is led by an elected Chief and Council and is focused on responsible governance, community wellbeing, and sustainable administration. As Gambler First Nation continues to strengthen its organizational capacity and financial stewardship, it is committed to transparent, accountable management of its resources in support of current community needs and future generations.

Download the Full Job Description: Gambler First Nation - Director of Finance - Position Profile.pdf

About The Director Of Finance Position

Reporting to the Chief and Council, the Director of Finance plays a critical leadership role in supporting the financial stewardship and long‑term sustainability of Gambler First Nation. This position is responsible for overseeing the Nation’s financial management, reporting, budgeting, and compliance functions while providing trusted advice to Chief and Council on financial strategy and decision‑making.

The Director of Finance ensures that financial practices align with legislative requirements, funding agreements, and sound governance principles, while also supporting operational leaders in managing programs and services effectively. The role balances strong technical financial expertise with a practical, community‑focused approach, recognizing the unique governance, funding, and accountability environment of a First Nation organization.

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Director of Finance contributes to organizational planning, risk management, and capacity building, and plays an important role in strengthening financial systems, controls, and reporting processes in support of transparency, accountability, and service to GFN members.

Gambler First Nation’s administrative office is transitioning from Russell, Manitoba, to Brandon, Manitoba, with the move anticipated by late Fall. The Director of Finance may work remotely, with an expectation of working in the Brandon office a minimum of two days per week once the Brandon office is fully operational.

Financial And Operational Accountabilities

Contribute to the development and execution of Gambler First Nation’s strategic and operational plans by providing financial leadership, analysis, and advice that supports community priorities and long‑term sustainability.
Lead the overall finance and accounting functions, including annual budgeting and forecasting, financial planning and analysis, reporting, capital planning, audits, insurance, asset management, cost control, and related financial activities.
Establish annual financial objectives that align with GFN’s strategic priorities, funding agreements, and governance expectations.

Education And Experience Requirements

Gambler First Nation is seeking a highly collaborative Director of Finance who values relationship‑building, teamwork, and shared accountability. This role is central to supporting the Nation’s long‑term financial sustainability and requires the ability to work closely and respectfully with Chief and Council, the Band Manager, program leaders, staff, external partners, and community stakeholders.

The Director of Finance is expected to build, lead, and sustain a high‑performing finance and administration function. Chief and Council and the organization will rely on the individual in this role for sound professional judgment, strategic financial advice, and technical expertise that supports effective governance and informed decision‑making.

The ideal candidate brings experience working in First Nations or Indigenous organizational environments and understands the governance, funding, and accountability context in which First Nation governments operate.

A post‑secondary degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field, combined with significant progressive experience in finance, accounting, and auditing, including senior‑level leadership of a finance function.
