Required experience in First Nations or Indigenous finance, including work within a First Nation government, Indigenous organization, tribal council, or Indigenous advisory or accounting services environment.

Experience

Proven experience in financial modelling, financial analysis, cash‑flow management, and the monitoring and management of investments.
Strong working knowledge of federal and provincial legislation, public policy, and funding frameworks applicable to First Nation governments and entities.
Proficiency with financial systems and tools or financial and reporting applications.

A highly collaborative leadership style, with the ability to work effectively across functions and build strong, respectful working relationships throughout the organization.

Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, including presentation and negotiation skills appropriate to executive and governance‑level settings.

About Toronto Metropolitan

For more than 75 years, Toronto Metropolitan University (formerly known as Ryerson University) has been shaping the next generation of leaders through its uniquely innovative, entrepreneurial and career-focused approach to higher education. Driven by bold leadership, cutting-edge research and a deep commitment to academic excellence, TMU collaborates with students, faculties, staff and partners to push boundaries, reimagine solutions and create meaningful change in an increasingly interconnected world.

For a more in-depth understanding of our vision, core values and ongoing work, please see our academic plan

TMU welcomes those who have demonstrated a commitment to upholding the values of equity, diversity, and inclusion and will assist us in realizing the benefits of embedding these values into the work at every level and in every unit of the university. In addition, to correct the conditions of disadvantage in employment in Canada and to bring lived experiences to the work, we encourage applications from members of equity deserving groups that have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples in Canada, First Nations Peoples in the United States, racialized people, Black people, persons with disabilities, women, and 2SLGBTQ+ people. Preference will be given to candidates with lived experiences as people from equity deserving groups, as well as experience working with these communities with which the University works every day. Please note that all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply and we welcome newcomers and immigrants to Canada.

In April 2022, the university announced its new name of Toronto Metropolitan University. Learn more about our next chapter.

About The School Of Medicine

It’s time to transform medical education. Toronto Metropolitan University’s School of Medicine has been designed from the ground up to shift the paradigm of healthcare delivery and improve the well-being of individuals, families and communities. With a community-driven, intentionally inclusive approach, the new school is training doctors whose cultural awareness and humility are as crucial as their medical skills.

Led by Dr. Teresa M. Chan, a forward-thinking educational leader, TMU’s School of Medicine draws on the university’s commitment to community, equity, and innovation to address rapidly changing healthcare needs. The school will train a new generation of physicians who are ready to learn, to adapt, and ultimately to be agents of change.

The Opportunity

We are hiring a Finance Director to join the School of Medicine! This newly created role leads the development and implementation of school-wide financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and resource management strategies that advance the academic, research, and operational priorities of the School of Medicine.

Serving as a trusted strategic advisor, the position provides expert financial counsel to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Dean, and senior leadership by assessing long-term financial implications, recommending evidence-based solutions, and ensuring alignment with broader University policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.

This role oversees the financial operations of the School of Medicine, supporting budgeting, reporting, financial compliance, and informed decision-making. he Director also provides financial and advisory support to the Integrated Health Centre, including support for external financial reporting and audit requirements,, in close collaboration with TMU Financial Services and the University Planning Office.

In addition, the Director conducts financial research and analysis to inform policy development and long-term planning, and represents the CAO and the School of Medicine in TMU-wide planning discussions and committees.

Responsibilities Include

Financial planning, budgeting and management

Provides financial advice, analysis, and decision-support to departments within the School of Medicine to support budget development, financial planning, forecasting, and effective resource management.
Manages day-to-day financial activities for the School of Medicine, including monitoring and reconciling operating and payroll expenditures, and ensures that actual financial results reconcile with approved targets
Collaborates with the University Planning Office (UPO) to support the annual budget development process for the SoM.

Payroll Administration and Financial Oversight (SoM Residents and IHC Employees)

Oversees, reviews, and approves biweekly payroll registers before the third-party vendor releases payments and monthly reconciliations. Investigate unusual variances, adjustments, and exceptions.
Monitors payroll funding requirements, forecast upcoming payroll obligations, and ensure sufficient funds are available in the designated bank account before each payroll withdrawal
Oversee the processes, systems, and internal controls supporting the administration of payroll, benefits, and expense claims for medical learners (residents) and Integrated Health Centre (IHC) staff.
Provide leadership and oversight to staff responsible for processing payroll, benefits, and expenses, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with applicable policies and requirements.
Establish and maintain effective procedures, workflows, and controls to support reliable and efficient administration of these functions.

Strategy and external collaboration

Conducts financial research and analysis to support the Dean and CAO in the development of a funding model for the School of Medicine and the Integrated Health Centres (IHC).
Monitors SOM activities relevant to external funding and reporting obligations, and ensures timely information sharing with relevant stakeholders.
Develops and implements a strategic roadmap for School-wide financial forecasting, planning, and internal financial controls, including long-term budget plan for the SoM that supports the academic, research, and operational priorities.
Provides expert analysis and strategic advice on financial risk management for proposed and approved School initiatives.

Financial evaluation and program analysis

Conducts financial evaluations of revenue-generating proposals and new initiatives, and analyzes program costing reports.

Accounting management, reporting & analysis

Manages a wide range of operating, trust, and project accounts (research and non-research) for the SoM and IHC.
Supports University-wide interim and year-end financial statement audits by coordinating SoM responses, and responds to audit inquiries related to IHC and SoM special purpose audits.
Leads the planning and execution of financial analysis to support strategic and operational decisions, and oversees the development and maintenance of statistical analysis systems and integrated financial tracking tools.

HR management

Manages and supervises staff, assigns and prioritises tasks, establishes goals, sets expectations and evaluates performance.

Qualifications

To help us learn more about you, please provide a cover letter and resume describing how you meet the following required qualifications:

Completion of a university degree program in finance, accounting, business or public administration, or a relevant field.
A minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in financial management within a post-secondary, public sector, or MUSH (municipalities, universities, school boards, hospitals) environment, including experience managing complex budgets, government funding, and resource planning.
Equivalent experience or a combination of equivalent experience and education may be accepted in place of education.
Demonstrated work experience in statistical analysis to support forecasting, financial modelling, and program/project viability assessments.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) is an asset.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including variance analysis and financial interpretation.
Knowledge of statistical analysis measurement theory to support forecasting, modelling, and program/project viability assessments.
In-depth knowledge of accounting and finance principles and associated technical and security considerations.
Knowledge of Microsoft Excel/Google Sheet and financial systems/software applications to support modelling and reporting.
Knowledge of post-secondary education systems, funding structures and sector-specific financial issues.
Demonstrated skill in developing and implementing financial policies, procedures and processes for new or evolving business initiatives.
Strong project and time management skills in a fast-paced environment.
Effective communication skills to convey complex financial information with stakeholders.
Troubleshooting skills, particularly in identifying causes of financial variances.
Ability to work on team-based projects, and prepare and present accurate reports to senior management.
Ability to organize and manage a complex financial process with accuracy and consistency.
Systems-wide thinking skills, with ability to assess financial and operational implications across units and stakeholder groups.

Leadership Competencies

Leaders at TMU are required to demonstrate the following Leadership Competencies:

jobs.title: IT Operations & Platform Director
jobs.description:
A propos de l'équipe

L’équipe TI et Transformation des Affaires
est une fonction mondiale relevant directement du PDG de Graitec. Elle est composée de quatre équipes : Transformation des Affaires, Données et IA, Sécurité de l’Information, et Opérations TI et Plateformes
. Ensemble, nous assurons les capacités opérationnelles qui permettent à Graitec de fonctionner efficacement et nous accompagnons sa transformation continue.

Nous travaillons en équipes fusionnées
, où les expert(e)s des affaires et des technologies collaborent autour d’objectifs communs et de résultats concrets.
L’équipe Opérations TI et Plateformes
soutient quotidiennement l’ensemble de l’organisation : plateformes d’affaires, infrastructure infonuagique, environnement numérique de travail et soutien aux utilisateurs. Son périmètre couvre notamment Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations
, Dynamics 365 CRM
, les outils de services professionnels, les systèmes RH, les plateformes clients et web, le centre de services TI, Microsoft Azure
, les réseaux et la gestion des identités. L’équipe dessert l’EMEA et l’Amérique du Nord et s’organise autour des domaines d’affaires qu’elle soutient.

Raison d’être du poste et contribution à la valeur d’affaires

Ce poste de direction est responsable de tout ce sur quoi les employés et les clients de Graitec comptent pour accomplir leur travail : les applications d’entreprise, l’infrastructure infonuagique et numérique ainsi que l’expérience globale de service TI.

Vous serez responsable de la qualité des services, de la fiabilité des plateformes, de la maîtrise des coûts et de la capacité de livraison. Plus qu’une fonction de soutien, vous agirez comme un partenaire stratégique auprès des équipes d’affaires, en bâtissant un environnement technologique agile, optimisé par l’IA et capable d’évoluer avec la croissance de l’entreprise.

Votre succès sera mesuré selon des indicateurs d’affaires tels que :

La productivité et l’expérience des employés;
La disponibilité, la performance et la résilience des plateformes;
L’optimisation des coûts opérationnels;
Les gains d’efficacité et d’échelle.

Ce que le succès représente dans les 12 premiers mois
Déployer un centre de services TI mondial axé sur l’expérience client, avec des niveaux de service publiés, un catalogue de services complet et des options libre-service largement adoptées. Les indicateurs de satisfaction (CSAT) et de recommandation (NPS) sont mesurés et en amélioration.
Assurer le soutien opérationnel complet du programme Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations
, avec un modèle d’exploitation et de soutien défini avant chaque mise en production.
Consolider l’environnement infonuagique et automatiser de bout en bout le cycle de vie des employés (arrivées, mobilités internes et départs).
Fournir une vision consolidée et fiable des coûts de plateformes, du positionnement des licences et de la performance des fournisseurs, tout en générant des économies.
Structurer les équipes comme une seule fonction intégrée, avec une taille optimale et une réduction des dépendances critiques.
Mettre en production une première vague d’initiatives d’IA et d’automatisation permettant de réduire les interventions manuelles et le volume de billets.
Renforcer la résilience opérationnelle grâce à des mécanismes éprouvés de sauvegarde et de relève informatique.

Responsabilités principales

Plateformes d’entreprise
Assurer la gestion complète du cycle de vie des plateformes d’entreprise : Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, CRM, solutions d’automatisation des services professionnels, systèmes RH et de paie ainsi que plateformes clients et web.
Collaborer avec l’équipe Transformation des Affaires pour assurer une transition harmonieuse des projets vers les opérations.
Travailler avec l’équipe Données et IA afin de garantir la qualité et la fiabilité des données.
Gérer les plateformes comme des produits : responsables identifiés, adoption mesurée et feuille de route alignée sur la valeur d’affaires.

Excellence des services TI
Développer une expérience de services TI mondiale alignée sur les meilleures pratiques ITIL et centrée sur l’utilisateur.
Définir et publier les niveaux de service et le catalogue de services.
Superviser la gestion des incidents, des problèmes et des changements à l’aide d’une plateforme ITSM moderne.
Assurer la gestion de l’environnement numérique de travail : Microsoft 365, Copilot, gestion des postes de travail et cycle de vie des employés.
Exploiter les données d’adoption et les commentaires des utilisateurs afin d’éliminer les causes récurrentes des demandes plutôt que de simplement les traiter.

IA et automatisation des opérations
Définir la stratégie d’intégration de l’IA au sein des opérations TI : résolution assistée ou automatisée, opérations auto-réparatrices et optimisation de l’environnement de travail numérique.
Collaborer avec les équipes Données et IA pour intégrer des solutions d’IA générant des bénéfices mesurables.
Mesurer et communiquer les gains obtenus : réduction des efforts manuels, diminution des délais de résolution et économies réalisées.

Infonuagique, infrastructure et résilience
Superviser les environnements Azure, les réseaux, la gestion des identités, les plateformes d’intégration et la modernisation des environnements existants.
Être responsable de la disponibilité, de la performance, de la sauvegarde, de la reprise après sinistre et de la résilience opérationnelle.
Promouvoir l’automatisation et l’infrastructure comme code afin de soutenir la croissance sans augmentation proportionnelle des effectifs.

Leadership et développement des équipes
Diriger et développer une équipe distribuée composée de gestionnaires d’infrastructure, de plateformes et de support.
Favoriser le développement des compétences, la relève et une culture d’imputabilité.
Accompagner les initiatives de gestion du changement pour assurer l’adoption des nouvelles façons de travailler.

Gestion des fournisseurs et des licences
Gérer les coûts des plateformes et de l’infrastructure, les licences et les relations avec les fournisseurs stratégiques.
Négocier les partenariats en fonction des résultats d’affaires recherchés.
Améliorer la transparence des coûts unitaires et démontrer les gains d’efficacité.
Construire les dossiers d’investissement pour les dépenses technologiques majeures et mesurer les bénéfices obtenus.

Sécurité de l’information et intégration d’acquisitions
Collaborer étroitement avec l’équipe Sécurité de l’Information afin d’intégrer les contrôles de sécurité, la gestion des accès, la conformité et les audits.
Soutenir les certifications telles que SOC 2 et ISO 27001.
Diriger l’intégration TI des acquisitions, de la préparation initiale à l’intégration complète dans l’architecture de l’entreprise.

Profil recherché

Expérience requise
Expérience significative à un poste de direction dans les opérations TI et la gestion d’applications d’entreprise dans un environnement international.
Expertise approfondie de l’écosystème Microsoft : Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, Dynamics 365 CRM, Microsoft 365, Azure, Entra ID et gestion moderne des postes de travail.
Expérience démontrée dans la mise en place de services TI orientés client et hautement performants.
Participation à des programmes majeurs de modernisation ERP et transition vers les opérations courantes.
Solide expérience de gestion des coûts, des licences, des fournisseurs et de l’intégration TI lors d’acquisitions.
Réalisations concrètes en matière d’IA et d’automatisation à grande échelle.
Capacité à interagir avec les équipes de direction et à présenter clairement les coûts, les risques, les bénéfices et le retour sur investissement.
Leadership calme et efficace en situation de crise ou lors d’incidents majeurs.

Atouts
Certification ITIL v4, TOGAF ou équivalent.
Certification PMP, PgMP ou équivalent.
Expérience dans un environnement multisociété et multinational.
Expérience au sein d’une entreprise en forte croissance, active en acquisition ou soutenue par du capital-investissement.

Processus d'entretien

Diversité et inclusion

Chez Graitec
, nous sommes fiers de promouvoir un milieu de travail inclusif où chacun peut être authentique et contribuer pleinement à notre succès. Nous accueillons les candidatures de toutes origines et évaluons chaque personne uniquement en fonction de ses compétences, de son expérience et de sa capacité à réussir dans le rôle.
Graitec utilise l’intelligence artificielle pour soutenir certains processus internes. Toutefois, toutes les décisions liées au recrutement, à l’évaluation des candidatures et à l’embauche sont prises exclusivement par notre équipe Acquisition de talents et nos gestionnaires recruteurs.
Processus de recrutement
Candidature
: Soumettez votre CV via le site Carrières de Graitec.
Entrevue RH
: Discussion exploratoire pour mieux vous connaître.
Entrevue avec le gestionnaire recruteur
: Échange approfondi sur le poste et votre expérience.
Entrevue avec des pairs ou partenaires d’affaires
: Peut inclure une présentation ou un exercice collaboratif.
Entrevue finale
: Rencontre avec le dirigeant de l’unité d’affaires.

Rémunération

Rémunération cible (OTE)

80 % salaire de base + 20 % rémunération variable

OTE minimum : 150 000 $ CAD

OTE maximum : 180 000 $ CAD

La fourchette salariale indiquée est présentée à titre informatif et correspond au niveau de séniorité visé pour ce poste.

The Opportunity

This is an 18-month fixed-term position covering a maternity leave. The Director, Financial Reporting, reporting to the Vice President of Finance, is a key member of the Finance department and owns the global financial close, consolidation, external financial reporting, and audit execution; and partners with internal stakeholders and external advisors on global tax compliance and planning. They are an experienced Controller/Director with extensive knowledge of accounting principles, systems and processes, and a passion for partnering with key stakeholders to drive awareness and optimization of the business. They are enthusiastic, high-energy, an experienced people leader, and passionate about coaching and investing in their team to elevate career development and experience.

This is a hands-on role in a high-growth software business backed by U.S. Private Equity. This role will partner with other senior leaders to continue to build and scale the department with best practices to support our global business with operations in Canada, US, UK, Romania and Australia.

What You'll Do

Financial Accounting and Reporting: Oversee the ongoing accounting function and financial reporting calendar to meet critical reporting timelines. Be the in-house technical accounting expert that ensures compliance with US GAAP (ASC 606 revenue recognition, ASC 718 stock based compensation, ASC 842 leases, etc), federal, state and local laws and accounting principles in the US, Canada, UK, LATAM, Romania, and Australia.
Audit Management: Manage the relationships with external auditors and government authorities. Effectively negotiate and defend the Company's accounting positions and manage audits to be on time and on budget. Prepare complex technical accounting and tax memos, working papers, and consolidated financial statements with note disclosures in compliance with US GAAP.
Tax: Participate in global tax planning and strategy (transfer pricing, SR&ED) and coordinate tax return compliance and preparation with our global tax advisors. Oversee sales tax compliance and follow-ups.
Collaborate with FP&A to support internal and external management reporting: Produce high-quality monthly, quarterly and annual consolidated financial statements, MD&A and management reports; provide thorough analysis of the financial data and effectively communicate key findings, opportunities and risk.
Lead AI-enabled finance automation across close, reconciliations, variance analysis, reporting, and audit support by integrating our tech stack (NetSuite, Concur, Salesforce, Adaptive Planning, UKG, Snowflake, and Claude) in partnership with AI/Systems, ensuring strong controls, data security, and documentation.

People Leader, Coach & Active Listener: Lead a team responsible for accounting, audit management, financial reporting and tax. Lead their training and development, performance evaluation and maintaining a healthy and collaborative work environment.

What You’ll Bring

CPA + experience at a top tier accounting firm + industry experience.
8 years' experience leading global accounting operations as a Controller/Director.
4 years of people management experience.
Advanced knowledge of US GAAP/IFRS.
Proficiency with NetSuite or similar ERP systems.
Experience preparing consolidated financial statements and note disclosures and managing auditors and government agencies.
Experience partnering with cross-functional stakeholders to drive results.
Egoless, Innovative and Entrepreneurial: Ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. Relentless focus on improvement and raising the bar. jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 274279

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Head of Global HR Analytics and Data Office leads and oversees a team comprised of the global data office; analytics and insights; advanced analytics capabilities; reporting and visualization; and AI. This role is the primary contact for all matters related to Global Human Resources data and is the champion for advancing analytics capabilities, technologies, human capital insights and a culture of data literacy.

As the Global Human Resources Data leader, this position oversees the data office and manages the design, development and implementation of data strategies; data standards; data products; data procedures; data governance; and data security all in alignment with the Bank’s data governance framework. This role is also accountable for developing and driving our advanced people analytics capabilities and to create data and analytics assets while advancing our behavioral science reach.

A key aspect of this role is to provide the experience and thought leadership to evolve our data strategy roadmap to achieve a consolidated and consistent global view of data across multiple systems and geographies. They will provide oversight and support for applied employee research, data mining, advanced analytics, and the development of predictive models to further our understanding of the workforce and improve employee experience.

This position is responsible for the production of all monthly, quarterly, annual, and ad-hoc human capital reporting requests and ensures the accuracy, comprehensiveness and timeliness of the data provided. Driving continuous improvement of self-serve and visualization capabilities is paramount in order to optimize user experience and adoption. They will also provide subject matter expertise and point of view on how to advance our technology capabilities such as AI, machine learning, large language models, and cloud-based tools.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:

Lead the transformation of Global HR’s data, analytics, reporting and visualization capabilities to improve data-driven decision making and accelerate insights at scale to help each line of business optimize human capital.
Drive applied employee research, data mining, analytical/statistical methodology, behavioral science and the development of predictive models to further our understanding of the workforce and enhance employee experience.
Lead advanced analytics to drive actionable insights to propel human capital decision making and build behavioral science capabilities to enhance employee understanding and awareness.
Partner closely with IT to develop data engineering pipelines, advance technology capabilities (i.e., software, infrastructure and data pipelines) to better leverage AI, machine learning and cloud-based tools.
Develop a programmatic approach to increase data literacy and adoption across Global Human Resources in order to enhance advice capabilities and to deliver impactful human capital insights for each line of business.
Manage the design, development and implementation of data strategies, data standards, data procedures, data governance and data security to support Global Human Resources and ensure alignment with the Bank’s Data Governance Framework.
Establish data quality rules, standards and thresholds and ensure appropriate data quality monitoring practices are in place; lead the identification and root-cause analysis of data quality issues and support remediation efforts in a timely manner based on priority.
Develop teams and create a high performing culture that nurtures talent and helps bring to life our values of collaboration, growth, and respect.
Manage direct reports and the broader department to achieve organizational goals in accordance with company policies and practices.
Create an effective work environment by developing a common vision, setting clear objectives, expecting teamwork, recognizing outstanding performance, maintaining open communications and encourage high level of engagement across the team.
Build a high-performance environment and implements a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops and motivates their team by fostering an inclusive work environment and using a coaching mindset and behaviors; communicating vison/values/business strategy; and, managing succession and development planning for the team.
Create an environment in which the team pursues effective and efficient operations of the respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values and Code of Conduct, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed? We’d love to work with you if you have:

Post-Secondary degree in a quantitative /computer science /data & analytics field. Relevant Master’s Degree is desirable. A minimum of seven or more years of progressive, relevant and practical experience in people analytics and data management; a proven track record of success in analytical reporting and the implementation/management of supporting technology systems.

At RBC Insurance, AI is fundamental to transforming how we operate, serve our customers, and compete in a rapidly evolving financial services landscape. What You'll Do

Enterprise Data & AI Strategy, Investment & Governance

Enterprise Standards: Establishes and approves enterprise standards for data architecture, quality, stewardship, interoperability, access, platforms and responsible AI, ensuring alignment with security, privacy, legal, clinical and regulatory requirements.
Decision Authority: Chairs or sponsors enterprise governance forums; resolves cross-enterprise priorities and trade-offs; and recommends whether initiatives should proceed, change course or stop based on strategic fit, risk, readiness and expected value.

Business Transformation, AI Adoption & Value Realization

Transformation Portfolio: Partners with executive and business leaders to identify and prioritize enterprise opportunities where data and AI can transform care delivery, client and employee experience, workforce capacity, productivity, quality, growth and financial performance.
Product and Delivery Accountability: Provides executive oversight for the end-to-end portfolio of analytics, automation and AI products, ensuring disciplined progression from discovery and experimentation through deployment, adoption, scaling and ongoing optimization.
Business Adoption: Establishes shared accountability with business owners for workflow redesign, change readiness, adoption and sustained use of data and AI capabilities across clinical and corporate functions.
Benefits Realization: Defines enterprise performance measures and holds the portfolio accountable for measurable clinical, operational, financial and strategic outcomes, including quality, safety, productivity, user adoption and return on investment.

Enterprise Risk, Privacy & Responsible AI

Risk Framework: Establishes the enterprise data and AI risk framework in partnership with Privacy, Legal & Compliance, Security, Clinical, Technology and other control functions, aligned with organizational risk appetite and regulatory obligations.
Responsible AI: Sets guardrails for ethical, transparent, explainable and equitable use of data and AI, including human oversight, bias monitoring, model validation, third-party risk and appropriate use of sensitive health information.
Executive Assurance: Provides executive visibility into material data and AI risks, control effectiveness, regulatory developments and emerging exposures, with clear recommendations and escalation pathways.
Ongoing Oversight: Ensures deployed data and AI products are monitored for safety, accuracy, security, performance, drift and unintended impacts, and initiates timely remediation where required.

Executive Partnership & Ecosystem Leadership

Executive Advisory: Serves as a trusted advisor to the Chief Digital Officer, CEO and senior leadership on enterprise data and AI strategy, investment choices, opportunities, risks and organizational readiness.
Enterprise Alignment: Builds shared ownership across clinical, operational, financial and corporate leaders and resolves competing priorities, dependencies and decision rights across the enterprise.
Commercial and Partner Strategy: Leads strategic vendor and partner relationships, including build-buy-partner decisions, commercial negotiations, performance governance, technology viability, cost optimization and responsible commercialization opportunities where appropriate.
External Leadership: Represents SE Health in relevant health-sector, technology, research and policy forums, strengthening strategic partnerships, sector influence and access to emerging capabilities.

People, Culture & Organizational Capability

Organizational Leadership: Designs and leads a high-performing, multidisciplinary Data & AI function with clear mandates, accountabilities, decision rights and performance expectations aligned to enterprise priorities.
Talent and Succession: Leads workforce planning, talent acquisition, leadership development, performance management and succession planning for critical data and AI capabilities, balancing internal capacity with strategic external expertise.
Enterprise Capability: Builds data literacy, responsible AI fluency and decision-making capability across the organization so leaders and teams can use data and AI confidently, safely and effectively.
Culture and Leadership: Fosters an inclusive, collaborative and accountable culture that encourages innovation, constructive challenge, continuous learning and disciplined execution.

What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, or a related quantitative field.
MBA or Master's degree in a related discipline considered an asset.(MS/MBA in Data Analytics, Computer Science, Business Analytics, or AI).
Relevant certifications considered an asset (e.g., Azure Data/AI Engineer, AWS Certified Machine Learning, Google Cloud Data Engineer, CIPP privacy certification, CDMP, or equivalent).
15+ years of progressive technology and data leadership experience, including senior executive accountability over enterprise data systems, business intelligence, data science, and enterprise platform delivery.
Demonstrated experience designing, building, and operating modern data stack architectures (Data Warehouses, Lakehouses, MLOps platforms) within complex enterprise environments.
Proven track record of deploying machine learning models, predictive tools, or Generative AI solutions into core production workflows to drive business value.
Demonstrated experience managing financial planning, cloud consumption/compute budgets, investment prioritization, and portfolio governance for data and AI programs.
In-depth knowledge of health data standards, data privacy laws (e.g., PHIPA, PIPEDA), clinical data structures, and ethical AI/governance frameworks.
Experience establishing data governance bodies, data stewardship programs, and enterprise data quality processes.

jobs.description:
Venor is proud to partner with Commissionaires Nova Scotia in the recruitment of a Chief Financial Officer.

Based in Bedford, Nova Scotia, Commissionaires Nova Scotia (CNS) is the province’s leading not-for-profit security provider, delivering guarding, monitoring, investigative, and specialized security services to more than 200 sites across the province. With roughly 1,300 employees, a large share of them veterans of the Canadian Armed Forces and RCMP, CNS is the largest private-sector employer of veterans in Nova Scotia. As part of the national Commissionaires federation of over 22,000 security professionals across Canada, CNS reinvests more than 90% of its annual revenue directly into employee wages, training, and benefits.

On their behalf, we are seeking a strategic and hands-on Chief Financial Officer to join the executive team. Reporting to the CEO, you will lead the organization’s financial strategy, reporting, planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, capital allocation, risk management, regulatory compliance, and governance. As a trusted advisor to the CEO, Executive Team, and Board of Governors, you’ll bring financial insight to strategic decision-making while leading a team of finance, IT, and procurement professionals and ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability.

What You’ll Be Doing

In this role, you’ll lead the organization’s financial strategy and provide executive-level financial advice across all business lines. You’ll develop, implement, and maintain financial policies, internal controls, and governance frameworks, and oversee financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, controllership, treasury management, and audit activities. You’ll also manage the enterprise financial systems and reporting platforms that keep the organization’s financial information timely and accurate, preparing and presenting financial reports to the CEO, Executive Team, Finance and Audit Committee, and Board of Governors, and developing the annual operating and capital budgets, including required submissions to Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).

You’ll provide strategic pricing guidance, including contract billing and labour rates, and ensure compliance with financial, regulatory, tax, and not-for-profit reporting requirements, including CRA obligations. Externally, you’ll manage relationships with financial institutions, auditors, insurers, the national Commissionaires federation, and government partners, and contribute to organizational strategy through financial analysis, business cases, and recommendations that support sustainable growth. Internally, you’ll provide executive oversight of payroll, compensation, benefits, and related financial administration, and lead, mentor, and develop a finance team spanning budgeting, payroll and accounts, IT/cyber, and procurement.

What You’ll Bring

You bring a Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field (or an equivalent combination of education and executive experience), along with a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing. You have 10+ years of progressive senior financial leadership experience, including strategic planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and governance within a complex organization, and a track record of advising executive teams, Boards of Directors or Governors, and senior stakeholders. Your knowledge of financial management, accounting standards, regulatory compliance, risk management, and corporate governance is strong, and you’ve demonstrated the ability to translate strategic priorities into measurable financial plans and business cases. You’ve led and developed high-performing finance teams, and you communicate complex financial information clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

The ideal candidate is a thoughtful, collaborative leader with strong business acumen and a genuine commitment to integrity, innovation, and service excellence. You’re as comfortable in the details of financial reporting as you are advising the boardroom, and you bring the judgment to manage competing priorities during budgeting, audit, and Board reporting cycles.

IPEX est l’un des principaux fournisseurs nord-américains de systèmes de canalisations en plastique de pointe. Notre mission est de façonner un avenir meilleur en reliant les collectivités à l’eau et à l’énergie
.

Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche d’un Directeur du programme PRE
pour se joindre à notre équipe. Ce poste est basé à Oakville (Ontario) ou Montréal (Québec)
et relève du vice-président, TI.

Ne manquez pas l’occasion de vous joindre à une équipe diversifiée de professionnels centrés sur l’humain, de leaders d’opinion, d’esprits novateurs et d’entrepreneurs qui remettent en question le statu quo.

Sommaire du poste

À titre de Directeur du programme PRE, vous serez responsable de la gouvernance et de l’exécution de bout en bout de l’écosystème ERP d’IPEX, avec une responsabilité particulière à l’égard du programme de transformation SAP S/4HANA. En étroite collaboration avec les dirigeants des secteurs d’affaires et des technologies de l’information, vous assurerez la réalisation d’une initiative stratégique d’envergure visant à soutenir les objectifs opérationnels et la croissance à long terme de l’entreprise.

Cette fonction représente une occasion unique de jouer un rôle de premier plan au sein de l’un des plus importants programmes de transformation technologique et organisationnelle d’IPEX. À la croisée des technologies, des opérations et de la gouvernance d’entreprise, vous veillerez à l’alignement des priorités d’affaires avec l’exécution du programme à l’échelle de notre réseau manufacturier nord-américain. La personne retenue possède une expertise approfondie de SAP, une solide expérience en gouvernance de programmes et la capacité de piloter des initiatives complexes dans un environnement en constante évolution.

Responsabilités principales

Assurer le succès du programme grâce à un partenariat tripartite structuré entre les TI, les unités d’affaires et l’intégrateur de systèmes, en définissant clairement les rôles, les droits décisionnels et les responsabilités à tous les niveaux de gouvernance.
Être responsable de l’atteinte des résultats d’affaires ciblés, de la réalisation des bénéfices attendus ainsi que de la stabilisation opérationnelle suivant les principales phases de déploiement et les mises en production.
Établir et appliquer les cadres de gouvernance du programme, incluant les points de contrôle, les comités de pilotage, les registres de risques et les mécanismes d’escalade.
Gérer les calendriers intégrés du programme, les plans de ressources, les risques, les interdépendances et les budgets excédant 10 M$.
Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires composées de plus de 50 employés internes et consultants externes.
Assurer la production des rapports destinés à la haute direction et au conseil d’administration, notamment les tableaux de bord de performance, les prévisions financières et le suivi des jalons stratégiques.
Établir et maintenir des relations de confiance avec les intégrateurs de systèmes et les fournisseurs stratégiques, tout en assurant le respect rigoureux des engagements contractuels, des échéanciers et des normes de performance.
Piloter les stratégies de préparation organisationnelle, de gestion du changement et de communication en partenariat avec les équipes responsables de la transformation et des affaires chez IPEX.
Promouvoir la standardisation des processus, la gouvernance des données et la gestion des données maîtres à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

Qualifications Et Expérience

Plus de 10 ans d’expérience progressive en leadership dans le domaine des technologies de l’information, dont un minimum de 5 ans dans des fonctions de direction associées à la livraison de programmes ERP.
Baccalauréat en technologies de l’information, en informatique, en génie ou en administration des affaires (obligatoire); MBA fortement souhaité.
Expérience éprouvée dans la conduite d’implantations complètes de SAP S/4HANA (greenfield ou brownfield) au sein d’environnements manufacturiers ou industriels.
Expérience de gestion de programmes ERP pluriannuels comportant des budgets supérieurs à 10 M$ et des équipes de plus de 50 personnes réparties sur plusieurs sites et plusieurs pays.
Excellente connaissance des modules SAP S/4HANA; familiarité avec SAP BTP ainsi qu’avec la gestion des versions et des environnements SAP.
Excellentes compétences en communication exécutive et capacité à vulgariser des concepts techniques complexes auprès de la haute direction et du conseil d’administration.
Solides aptitudes en négociation, en gestion de fournisseurs et en influence au sein d’environnements matriciels.
Capacité démontrée à évoluer dans l’ambiguïté, à prendre des décisions sous pression et à instaurer un climat de confiance auprès d’équipes multidisciplinaires.
Aptitude à diriger des transformations organisationnelles d’envergure en favorisant l’adhésion, l’alignement et l’engagement des parties prenantes.
Expérience démontrée dans l’atteinte des résultats convenus, la réalisation des bénéfices escomptés, l’amélioration de la performance opérationnelle et l’atteinte des objectifs du programme.
Capacité à identifier, évaluer et atténuer les risques de façon proactive tout en assurant l’efficacité des mécanismes de gouvernance et d’escalade.
Engagement envers l’innovation, l’optimisation des processus et l’excellence opérationnelle afin de maximiser la valeur d’affaires et les capacités de la plateforme ERP.

Mobilité

Une mobilité est requise selon les besoins de l'entreprise et les étapes clés du programme, incluant des visites dans les installations d'IPEX, sur les sites de projets et auprès de partenaires, au besoin.

Purpose

As the Director of Commercial Pricing and Data Governance at UNFI, you are responsible for developing and executing the company's enterprise-wide pricing strategy while leading the Data Governance function. Your role is critical in driving commercial excellence, ensuring data integrity, and enabling informed business decisions across the organization.

In the area of pricing, your scope includes building and leading a centralized pricing department that will define, govern, and continuously improve UNFI Canada’s brand and customer pricing strategy. This role will move the organization toward a more disciplined pricing model, shifting pricing ownership away from Sales over time so that Sales can remain focused on customer relationships, execution of brand strategies, and commercial growth. You will immediately assume leadership of pricing activities currently managed within SRM and RGM, while developing the structure, tools, processes, resource requirements, governance model, and transition plan required to bring Sales pricing responsibilities into the pricing organization in the medium term. You will establish clear decision-making protocols, pricing guardrails, escalation processes, analytical capabilities, and best practices to support consistent, data-driven pricing decisions that improve margin performance, strengthen customer and supplier strategies, and deliver both immediate and long-term revenue value.

In the area of Data Governance, you will lead the Retalix Pricing, Retalix Maintenance, and MCB teams. You are accountable for ensuring data quality, governance, and integrity across Supplier Services, including pricing updates, GS1 data management, new brand onboarding information, and system master data maintenance. Your leadership will ensure that core data processes are effectively managed and aligned with business and operational requirements.

By partnering closely with cross-functional teams and senior leaders, you will enable the successful execution of UNFI's strategic priorities through the effective use of data and analytics. You will foster a culture of accountability, agility, and data-driven decision-making while ensuring alignment with UNFI's vision and objectives. Ultimately, your role is to drive sustainable revenue growth, improve profitability, and maximize the value of data as a strategic asset across the organization.

Lead Pricing Strategy (50%)

Develop the brand and customer pricing strategy for UNFI Canada
Review and optimize our current pricing tools and governance
Immediately take on SRM/RGM pricing and bring forward the recommendation (inclusive of tools and resources) to take pricing on from the sales team
Establish and enforce guardrails, policies, and pricing strategies to ensure adherence to revenue targets, margin optimization, and overall revenue growth.
Serve as a subject matter expert and provide deep understanding of customer economics, supplier dynamics, and market sensitivities to enable win-win pricing and solution proposals.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Sales, Supplier Services, Marketing, Operations, Supply Chain, Legal, Finance, and IT, to address executional barriers, develop innovative pricing solutions, and align strategies with organizational objectives and initiatives.
Collect and communicate IT business requirements and play key role in deployment of technical and system enhancements to ensure minimal risk to internal and external customers

jobs.title: Director, Fraud Analytics & Risk Management
jobs.description:
At Manulife Bank, protecting our customers, advisors, and business from financial crime is a critical strategic priority. As Director, Fraud Analytics & Risk Management, you will lead the Bank's fraud analytics and intelligence capabilities, leveraging advanced data analytics, customer risk modeling, and fraud technologies to proactively identify, detect, and mitigate fraud across all banking products, channels, and customer journeys.

This role is responsible for developing a data-driven fraud management ecosystem that delivers strong customer protection while enabling frictionless banking experiences. Working closely with Operations, Risk, Technology, Digital, Data & Analytics, and external partners, you will drive innovative solutions that enhance fraud detection, strengthen customer risk management, and improve fraud prevention outcomes.

Reporting to the AVP/VP, Fraud Strategy & Operations, you will play a key leadership role in shaping the future state fraud capability at Manulife Bank.

Position Responsibilities

Lead Fraud Analytics & Intelligence

Develop and execute the Bank's fraud analytics strategy across deposits, lending, mortgages, payments, digital banking, contact centre, and advisor channels.
Establish proactive monitoring and analytical capabilities to detect emerging fraud risks, customer scams, account takeover attacks, identity theft, synthetic identities, mule activity, and organized fraud networks.
Leverage internal and external data sources to identify fraud trends, vulnerabilities, and opportunities for control enhancement.
Lead fraud intelligence and root-cause analysis activities to continuously improve detection and prevention effectiveness.
Build meaningful analytics, dashboards, and executive reporting to support fraud management decision-making.

Own Customer Risk Scoring & Fraud Decisioning

Design, develop, and continuously optimize customer fraud risk scoring models across the customer lifecycle.
Enhance risk-based authentication, transaction monitoring, and fraud intervention strategies.
Leverage behavioural analytics, device intelligence, digital signals, transaction patterns, and external intelligence to improve customer risk segmentation.
Monitor model performance and ensure appropriate governance, oversight, validation, and recalibration.
Support development of real-time fraud detection and decisioning capabilities as the Bank evolves its payments and digital banking ecosystem.

Advance Fraud Technology Capabilities

Lead evaluation, implementation, and optimization of fraud technology solutions that strengthen the Bank's fraud prevention capabilities.
Partner with vendors to implement prevention and detection fraud toolkits
Develop business cases and strategic recommendations for fraud technology investments.
Manage vendor relationships, performance expectations, and ongoing solution effectiveness reviews.

Strengthen Fraud Risk Management

Lead comprehensive fraud risk assessments across products, processes, channels, and strategic initiatives.
Partner with Enterprise Risk Management and Compliance teams to ensure fraud risks are appropriately identified, measured, monitored, and mitigated.
Define and maintain fraud risk indicators, thresholds, risk appetite metrics, and reporting frameworks.
Identify control gaps and drive remediation strategies.
Support regulatory, audit, and governance reviews related to fraud risk management.

Enable Data-Driven Fraud Prevention

Partner with Analytics on developing predictive models to improve fraud detection and prevention outcomes.
Leverage machine learning, network analytics, behavioural analytics, anomaly detection, and AI-enabled capabilities where appropriate.
Balance fraud loss reduction objectives with customer experience considerations.
Translate complex analytical findings into actionable business recommendations for senior leadership.

Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team

Build and lead a team of fraud analytics, fraud intelligence, and risk professionals.
Foster a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, accountability, and customer focus.
Coach and develop talent while building future fraud analytics capabilities for the Bank.
Serve as a trusted advisor to executives and stakeholders on fraud risk trends, emerging threats, and mitigation strategies.

Required Qualifications

University degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Business, Finance, Risk Management, or a related discipline.
10+ years of experience in fraud analytics, fraud risk management, financial crimes, banking analytics, or advanced data analytics.
Deep understanding of fraud risks across retail banking products and customer journeys.
Experience developing fraud detection models, customer risk scoring frameworks, and fraud monitoring programs.
Experience managing fraud technology vendors and implementing fraud

Preferred Qualifications

Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills.
Graduate degree in a quantitative or business discipline. Professional certifications such as:
Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE)
Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS)
Certified Analytics Professional (CAP)
Experience with machine learning and AI-enabled fraud detection solutions.
Experience supporting real-time payments, digital banking, and emerging payment ecosystems.
Experience working with SQL, Python, SAS, Power BI, Tableau, machine learning and predictive analytics tools, fraud detection and case management platforms, identity verification technologies, behavioural analytics solutions, and device intelligence platforms to support data-driven decision-making, fraud prevention, and operational effectiveness.

Success in This Role

You Will Be Successful If You

Demonstrate strategic thinking and strong business acumen.
Drive measurable improvements in fraud control effectiveness.
Proactively identify emerging fraud risks before they impact customers.
Build strong partnerships across the Bank and Enterprise.
Translate complex fraud risks into actionable business recommendations.
Balance customer experience, operational efficiency, regulatory requirements, and risk management objectives

jobs.title: Senior Director, Chapter Lead, Insurance Analytics
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

As a member of CIBC’s AI, Data and Analytics team, the Senior Director – Decision Science will lead the Insurance Decision Science team and be responsible for developing and executing strategic initiatives across a range of CIBC Insurance products and projects. This is a senior technical leadership role that combines actuarial, statistical, data science and AI enablement capabilities. The role naturally involves a comprehensive understanding of Creditor (Bank Authorized) and Non-Authorized insurance products. You’ll exercise a high degree of independent judgement, setting the technical direction and standards for decision science activities that support pricing, profitability, growth, forecasting, portfolio performance and strategic decision making. You will develop and maintain trusted relationships across the Insurance business, larger Retail Banking organization and the technology and data science communities. In addition, you’ll translate sophisticated analysis of complex business information into clear recommendations for executives and business leaders, while providing independent challenge to assumptions, forecasts and proposed courses of action. You’ll drive innovation across areas of your responsibility and apply expert interpersonal, communication and problem-solving skills.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Strategy and Planning – Contribute to long-term strategy for the business in collaboration with insurance product and business leaders. Translate actuarial and advanced analytics into decisions on pricing, profitability, growth, forecasting and portfolio performance; identify opportunities, develop strategic proposals and independently challenge key assumptions and targets. Collaborate with internal partners to oversee, communicate and align business plans and ensure delivery on strategy and intended business outcomes.
Technical Skills - Set and maintain standards for actuarial, statistical, data science and AI-enabled methods, models, tools and controls. Apply quantitative methods to identify, assess and validate the drivers of profitability, growth, market share, portfolio performance and risk exposure, and synthesize complex analysis to influence business decisions and outcomes. Establish forward-looking performance measurement, forecasting, product analysis and decision-support capabilities that enable timely action, rather than reporting results alone.
People Management - Own the team’s capability and talent strategy, including workforce planning, succession, hiring, development, coaching and deployment of actuarial and analytics talent against business priorities. Build differentiated technical capabilities, establish clear role and proficiency standards, and create development pathways that strengthen the team over time. Manage capacity to ensure initiatives are appropriately staffed, identify capability gaps and remove obstacles to performance. Create a positive work environment and role model by championing CIBC’s mission, vision and values. Comply with policies, standards, guidelines and controls by applying them fairly and consistently so employees understand what to expect.

Who You Are

You are a senior actuarial and analytics leader with strong quantitative knowledge and relevant industry experience. You are an actuary, and hold an advanced degree an actuarial, data science, analytics or related technical field, or equivalent experience, and bring senior-level experience in insurance.
You have a high degree of Insurance product knowledge and understand the regulatory landscape. You have expert knowledge of insurance products (both authorized and non-authorized), banking and insurance frameworks, and the risk and compliance considerations that shape product decisions.
You can demonstrate extensive experience in product management, strategic planning, and project management sufficient to identify, develop, and implement approved initiatives. You have strong analytical, problem-solving skills, excellent communication and presentation skills sufficient to prepare and present material to an executive audience.
You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems, and making sense of information. You're confident in your ability to communicate detailed information in an impactful way.
You’re an effective leader and collaborator. You build strong relationships across teams, use sound judgment, manage multiple priorities effectively and help create an environment where people can do their best work. You are a technical leader, not a distant administrator. You remain intellectually engaged in the methods, systems, and decisions that determine whether the work succeeds.
You act like an owner. You thrive when you're empowered to take the lead, go above and beyond, and deliver results.
Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.

Position Overview

The Senior Director, Data Platform will lead Zynga's centralized data platform and product strategy, managing one of the largest data footprints in the gaming industry—billions of daily gameplay events flowing through a cloud-native stack spanning real-time ingestion, a petabyte-scale warehouse, experimentation, and a self-serve metrics and AI platform. Operating with high autonomy and direct executive sponsorship, you will act as a pathfinder: empowering our global studios to extract maximum value from central data and transforming the group to an AI-first way of working. This highly visible role is based in Toronto and partners closely with studio leaders, central teams, and executives across Zynga's global labels. Relocation support is available.

Highly technical product leaders on the data side are also encouraged to apply.

Familiarity with modern LLM and agentic patterns (RAG, semantic layers, MCP-style tooling) is a strong need. This is a critical, non-negotiable requirement.
Platform depth: Demonstrated ownership of large-scale, cloud-native data platforms on AWS—modeling, batch and streaming pipelines, cost/performance optimization, reliability (SLOs, observability), and data quality at scale.
Semantic layer & governance: Experience scaling semantic/metrics layers and self-serve analytics (dbt, metrics stores, Tableau/Lightdash) and familiarity with experimentation platforms and data privacy/compliance frameworks.
Cross-functional leadership: Comfort managing non-engineering functions (Product and Production) and translating technical concepts into clear business value for executives and non-engineers.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Data Governance
jobs.description:
About QuadReal Property Group

QuadReal Property Group is a global real estate investment, development and operating company headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its assets under management are $98.5 billion. From its foundation in Canada as a full-service real estate operating company, QuadReal has expanded its capabilities globally for investments in equity and debt in both the public and private markets. QuadReal invests directly through operating platforms in which it holds an ownership interest and via programmatic partnerships.

QuadReal seeks to deliver strong investment returns while creating sustainable environments that bring value to the people and communities it serves. Now and for generations to come.

QuadReal: Excellence lives here.

www.quadreal.com

Role Description

The Director, Enterprise Data Governance is accountable for defining and governing the enterprise data QuadReal relies on, anchored in DAMA-DMBOK, covering data definitions, ownership, quality, and observability. This makes QuadReal's data reliable enough to be governed, measured, and controlled, reducing the risk that decisions, reporting, and controls rest on data that can't be trusted. The role reports to the VP, Risk & Integrated Assurance and turns the VP's enterprise-wide mandate into one accountable operating model focused on risk mitigation through data governance lens.

Success is measured by the risk it mitigates: data issues caught before they become decisions made on incorrect information, ownership gaps closed before they become accountability gaps. Holding up under audit is one key aspect of that risk mitigation but not the goal in itself.

The Director also supports the VP's overall view of QuadReal's risk and control environment and represents Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Governance
Define QuadReal’s enterprise data definitions, classifications, and Critical Data Elements (CDEs), anchored in DAMA-DMBOK.
Own the data ownership and accountability model: name Data Owners, Stewards, and Custodians, and hold them accountable through a defined sign-off cadence.
Deliver the enterprise business glossary under a tiered governance model, and maintain metadata management, lineage standards, and dbt metadata synchronization across the platform.
Set data quality thresholds and Trusted Layer certification criteria, and hold data observability (freshness, pipeline health, trust scores) to the same standard as financial controls.
Align controls as gates across the data delivery lifecycle (ingestion, definition, build, use, and govern), so a control fires wherever data advances and nothing reaches a certified output without passing.
Build data governance capability across the business through training and playbooks, rather than keeping expertise centralized.
Integration and Decision Authority
Act as the link between Business Controls and Data Governance called for in the integrated operating model: define control standards and evidence expectations alongside data definitions, and build controls into new systems and initiatives from the start.
Where control standards and data definitions conflict, collaborate with relevant stakeholders including, ED&A, Business Owners and Business Controls to resolve these inconsistencies. Work with ED&A / Technology and the Data Platform team so controls and governance are proactively built into the toolchain (Microsoft Fabric, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Purview, Entra ID, Quadrant) by design.
Represent Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance meetings and support Audit Committee reporting.
Team Leadership
Lead and develop direct report(s) and set clear deliverables and cadence for them..
Build team capability in data analytics, AI literacy, and integrated systems controls as the role grows, and build bench strength to move the environment from project to sustained run-state without single points of failure.
Build a “one team” culture between Business Controls and Data Governance that removes duplicate work and closes the gaps that used to sit between the two groups.

What Success Looks Like

Controls operating as gates, each with a named owner and re-performable evidence.
Audit outcomes: clean walkthroughs, deficiencies remediated, and SOC scope defensible.
Glossary and standards adopted, so certified numbers are built on agreed definitions.
Governance measured by delivery: trusted, in-use data products standing behind reported figures.
Direct reports delivering to plan, with growing capability and bench strength.

Qualifications

jobs.description:
Position:
Vice President – Governance & Reporting, Internal Audit
Location:
Montreal

About Us

The Maples Group is a global leader in financial services, trusted by many of the world’s largest hedge fund managers, private equity firms, and international corporations.
Our side-by-side financial and legal teams consistently deliver award-winning services to a global client base, offering unrivalled learning and career opportunities to our 2,500 colleagues worldwide. With 18 locations across the Americas, Asia, Europe and the Middle East, our international presence offers a unique springboard for career development and cross- cultural immersion.

What’s it like to work here?

We are driven to excel, and collaboration is key to our continued success. We can go further for our clients because we go further for each other too. We are committed to diversity, inclusion and equal of opportunity as we attract, retain and develop world-class talent. Our inclusive culture creates an environment where people can be themselves at work while doing their best work. No matter where you work in the Maples Group, you will be part of a global team.

The Opportunity

The Maples Group is seeking a Vice President – Governance & Reporting to join our Internal Audit team in Montreal. This is newly created leadership role is responsible for designing, executing and continuously enhancing the governance, reporting and quality-assurance framework for our global Internal Audit function. Acting as a key architect of our third line of defence, the successful candidate will ensure that Internal Audit delivers clear, timely and data-driven insight to the Audit Committees and key stakeholders, while aligning with the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) global Internal Audit Standards.

Consistently recognised as one of Montreal’s Top Employers, the Maples Group established our operations in the central downtown area in 2009. Our Montreal office exemplifies our culturally rich and entrepreneurial organisation, with over 300 colleagues from 50 countries collaborating to deliver best-in-class solutions to clients worldwide.

Reporting directly to the Senior Vice-President, you will:

Own the end-to-end Internal Audit governance calendar, including timely preparation and delivery of reporting packs for audit meetings
Produce concise, visually engaging dashboards on audit plan delivery, thematic issues, outstanding audit findings, emerging risks and quality metrics for senior stakeholders and the Audit Committees
Design, implement and maintain a comprehensive Quality Assurance and Improvement Programme (QAIP) in line with the IIA Standards and local regulatory requirements
Govern the creation, periodic review and formal approval of audit methodology (IA Charter, Internal Audit Procedures Manual, templates and guidance notes) ensuring timely updates for regulatory and professional-standards changes
Operate the escalation framework for delays, scope changes and impediments, ensuring early and transparent communication
Track and report on audit findings, actions and remediation progress
Manage the automation agenda for Internal Audit, including digitisation of audit processes and report templates, exploration of automation technologies, and enhancement of risk-rating methodologies through data analytics and predictive indicators
Serve as Internal Audit’s primary liaison on governance and quality matters with senior management, risk and compliance heads, and external auditors; present complex technical concepts in a clear, business-oriented manner tailored to diverse audiences

Whilst governance and reporting are the primary functions of this role, the candidate may be requested to assist with or conduct audit engagements.

What You Bring

In addition to indisputably high ethical standards and autonomy, the ideal candidate possesses the following:
A minimum of 5 years’ experience in internal audit within financial services or a similarly regulated environment
Proven expertise in designing and operating an Internal Audit quality-assurance framework; prior responsibility for a QAIP or equivalent is strongly preferred
Strong knowledge of the IIA Standards and associated guidance
Demonstrated success in governance reporting to boards of directors, Audit Committees and regulators, with superior written and verbal communication skills

Key skills and qualifications for this role are as follows:

Attention to detail, professionalism and a team first mentality
Experience with data-analytics and automation tools; ability to translate technology opportunities into practical efficiency gains
Strong understanding of risk and control assessment techniques, risk taxonomies and audit-universe construction
Highly organised self-starter, capable of working independently, managing multiple priorities and influencing without direct authority
Excellent time management, organisational, prioritisation and communication skills (fluent written and oral English)

Benefits & Rewards

The most enduring professional relationships are reciprocal relationships. The Maples Group prioritises employee health and wellbeing. We offer a range of benefits, including:

Comprehensive health coverage (medical, dental and optical)
Competitive vacation packages
Educational assistance and professional development programs
Savings or pension plan
Life insurance
Travel insurance
Global mental wellness program
Social events

Disclaimer:
All personal information collected during the application process will be used for recruitment-related purposes only. Please refer to our Job Applicant Privacy Notice at maples.com/privacy for details on how we handle personal information relating to job applicants.

“Please note that it is the Maples Group standard policy to undertake various background screening checks on all applicants to whom a conditional job offer is made. Except for roles based in the Republic of Ireland, the background checks will include criminal records checks when a conditional job offer is made. If you have a criminal record, it does not mean that your job offer will be automatically withdrawn. The Maples Group will make all job offer decisions on a case-by-case basis and will take a number of factors into account, such as the role that you are applying for and the nature and circumstances of the past offence. You will have the opportunity to discuss the matter with us before a decision is made. Further details will be provided at the time any conditional job offer is made.”

Poste :
Vice-président – Gouvernance et production de rapports, Audit interne
Emplacement :
Montréal

À propos de nous

Le Groupe Maples est un leader mondial des services financiers auquel font confiance de nombreux gestionnaires de fonds de couverture, sociétés de capital-investissement et entreprises internationales parmi les plus importants au monde.
Nos équipes financières et juridiques, qui travaillent côte à côte, fournissent constamment des services primés à une clientèle mondiale, offrant ainsi des possibilités d’apprentissage et de carrière inégalées à nos 2 500 collègues dans le monde. Répartie dans 18 régions en Amérique, en Asie, en Europe et au Moyen-Orient, notre présence internationale offre un tremplin unique pour le perfectionnement professionnel et l’immersion interculturelle.

L’occasion

Nous recherchons un Analyste des données et des rapports
accompli pour se joindre à notre équipe au sein de notre activité de services financiers à Montréal.

Constamment reconnu comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs de Montréal, le Groupe Maples a établi ses activités dans le centre-ville en 2009. Notre bureau de Montréal illustre bien la richesse culturelle et l’esprit d’entreprise de notre organisation, avec plus de 300 collègues de 50 pays qui collaborent pour fournir des solutions de premier ordre à des clients du monde entier.

Vos principales responsabilités comprennent :

relevant directement du vice-président, le candidat retenu participera au soutien opérationnel quotidien de nos clients institutionnels;
l’analyste principal des données et des rapports sera responsable du soutien de tous les aspects de la comptabilité et du rendement du portefeuille, ainsi que des éléments d’analyse et de refonte des processus;

traduire les exigences de l’entreprise en spécifications techniques pour les développeurs;
participer à divers projets de nature technique;
remplir des rapports périodiques sur la réglementation et les risques pour un ensemble diversifié de clients.

Outre un engagement à offrir une expérience supérieure aux candidats et aux parties prenantes :
le candidat idéal sera titulaire d’un diplôme universitaire en finance ou en comptabilité;
au moins deux à trois ans d’expérience professionnelle dans le domaine de la finance ou des services financiers;
une expérience en comptabilité ou en administration de fonds, un atout;
de solides compétences sur les plans des techniques et des systèmes
de l’expérience en gestion des relations et en service client.

Les principales compétences pour ce poste sont les suivantes :

solide connaissance de Microsoft Excel, y compris les macros VBA;
SQL ou autres langages de programmation, un atout;
connaissance du cadre de gestion de projet;
