About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most
. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster
by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 30,000 locations across 32+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

The Role

Solink is at an inflection point in our growth journey. As Chief Financial Officer, you'll lead our financial strategy as we continue to scale and prepare the company for its next chapter of growth.

This is a critical leadership role, shaping both the day-to-day financial operations and the long-term strategic direction of the company. You'll bring a strong operational and strategic background, proven success scaling technology businesses, and the judgment to know when to zoom in on the details and when to zoom out to see the bigger picture.

What You'll Do

Lead the Finance Team: Oversee and develop the leaders of Solink’s FP&A and Accounting functions. Set clear priorities, strengthen collaboration between the teams, and hold them accountable for accurate, timely work and useful business insights.
Get Close to the Work: Understand how financial work gets done today, identify where processes break down, and work alongside the team to fix them. Bring the judgment and willingness to dig into details that a growing business needs.
Improve Processes and Systems: Simplify and document core finance processes, improve data quality, and introduce automation where it reduces manual work and errors. Build a function that can scale without relying on workarounds or individual heroics.
Strengthen Planning and Decision-Making: Guide the established FP&A function in delivering reliable budgets, forecasts, financial models, and analysis. Partner with leaders across Solink to turn that work into clear decisions and accountability for results.
Build Trust in Financial Reporting: Lead the Accounting function through a strong close, audit, and reporting cadence. Strengthen internal controls and ensure compliance with applicable GAAP/IFRS requirements while giving leaders confidence in the numbers.
Support Capital Strategy and Investor Relationships: Partner with the CEO and Board on financial strategy, capital needs, financing opportunities, and investor communications. Ensure Solink has the financial discipline and information needed to evaluate future opportunities.
Evaluate Strategic Opportunities: Assess potential acquisitions and partnerships, including due diligence, financial modelling, and the practical work required to integrate them successfully.

Role Expectations

This is an E3 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level own company-wide outcomes, set the strategy for their function, and operate with broad autonomy in partnership with the CEO, the executive team, and the Board.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

Act as a full strategic partner to the CEO and the Board, not only as a steward of the numbers.
Build and develop a finance organization that scales ahead of the business, hiring and coaching leaders who raise the bar.
Bring financial discipline to company-wide decisions on pricing, investment, headcount, and market expansion.
Own the accuracy and credibility of forecasting, reporting, and board materials.
Prepare the company for its next financing or strategic event well before it is needed.

What success looks like:

Forecasting and planning the executive team and Board trust and act on.
The systems, controls, and team in place to operate credibly at $200M+ in revenue.
Solink positioned and diligence-ready for its next strategic chapter.

What You Bring

Must-Have:

10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, with prior scale-up CFO experience.
Proven track record scaling SaaS or technology companies from ~$50M to $200M+ revenue, with experience navigating different exit paths.
Deep FP&A expertise with strong analytical and strategic planning capabilities.
Direct experience with late-stage fundraising (Series C/D/E) or public markets experience.
Strong command of SaaS metrics and recurring revenue models.
Knowledge of GAAP/IFRS, compliance frameworks, and audit oversight.
Inspirational leader with the ability to develop high-performing finance teams.

Nice-to-Have:

M&A experience across due diligence, valuation, and post-close integration.
Experience in a Canadian company with US and international operations, including multi-currency and cross-border tax considerations.

Security Requirements

Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;
Be a Canadian or American Citizen, or eligible to work in Canada or the United States.
Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

Our Values

We do things the Solink way:

Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.
Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.
Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.
Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.

Why Solink?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.
Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.
Comprehensive benefits: A stellar benefits package, ensuring you're fully supported with anything you need.
Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.
Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.
Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.
Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.

What To Expect From The Hiring Process

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

Intro Call with Our Talent Team
Interview with the Hiring Manager
Interview with Senior Director, People & Culture and Chief Corporate & Legal Officer (Individual 45-Minute Slots)
Final Interviews with Two Board Members
Reference Checks
Offer & Onboarding

Please note: this is subject to change at any point in the recruitment process based on the needs of the business.

How To Apply

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our [Careers Page]. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of the Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.

Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.

Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls

Qualifications

10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business
strongly preferred.

Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience in a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.

Financial and commercial acumen

Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, this role will translate complex financial and operational data into actionable insights that support executive decision-making and long-term sustainability. The successful candidate will oversee budgeting, forecasting, scenario modelling, and financial performance analysis while strengthening resource allocation and financial accountability. Working closely with senior leaders, country teams, and cross-functional stakeholders, the Director will help align organizational strategy with operational priorities and available resources. This position also offers the opportunity to modernize financial systems, improve reporting capabilities, and build a high-performing international FP&A team. Accountabilities

Lead the annual consolidated budget, rolling forecasts, multi-year financial plans, and in-year reforecasting across countries, departments, programs, and funding sources.
Develop integrated financial and operational models connecting program reach, cost per beneficiary, staffing, capital needs, funding availability, and cash requirements.

Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear recommendations, identify risks and opportunities, and influence decision-making.

IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Vice President, Finance & Facilities

Reports to EVP Corporate Services

100% virtual

12-15 month engagement

Our client is a highly reputable Canadian organization
with a significant and multifaceted mandate. During a period of leadership transition, they are seeking an accomplished Interim Vice President, Finance & Facilities
to provide stability, strong financial stewardship and experienced leadership while helping position the organization for its next chapter.

This is more than a maintenance assignment. It is an opportunity for an experienced finance executive to come in, make an immediate impact and elevate an already high-performing function
. The successful interim will inherit a capable team and will be expected to provide visible leadership, bring fresh perspective, strengthen financial insight and discipline, and identify opportunities to enhance the sophistication and effectiveness of the function.
The mandate spans financial reporting, planning, performance management, risk and controls, treasury, facilities and procurement, while providing senior leadership with thoughtful financial advice and insight.

The Mandate

Working closely with the senior executive team, the Interim VP will take leadership of the finance function and ensure continued strength in the organization's financial management during the transition.

This is a role for someone equally comfortable around the executive table and in the details
. The successful executive will be strategic when the situation requires it, but willing to roll up their sleeves, challenge assumptions, solve problems and help the team execute.

Key priorities will include:

Providing strong financial stewardship
, ensuring the continued integrity, accuracy and timeliness of financial reporting, forecasting and financial operations.
Leading and supporting a strong finance team, creating clarity, engagement and momentum through a period of change.
Acting as a trusted financial advisor to senior leadership, bringing insight to organizational performance, longer-term planning and decision-making.
Reviewing existing financial processes, controls and practices and identifying opportunities to modernize, streamline and elevate the sophistication of the function.
Providing leadership across facilities management and procurement, ensuring strong governance, commercial discipline and effective execution.
Strengthening budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow planning, risk management and performance reporting.
Working effectively with external advisors, auditors and other key stakeholders.
Supporting senior leadership and the organization's governance bodies with credible, thoughtful financial insight. The underlying position specifically supports Audit and Finance Committee and Board activities.
Looking beyond business-as-usual to identify opportunities to drive change, improve effectiveness and leave the organization stronger at the conclusion of the mandate.

The Ideal Interim Executive

We are looking for a seasoned financial executive who knows how to enter an established organization, quickly understand the environment and add value without unnecessary disruption
.

Ideally, this individual will bring a combination of not-for-profit and commercial experience
, pairing an understanding of stewardship, governance and stakeholder accountability with the commercial instincts and operational discipline of the private sector.

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant senior financial leadership experience within a complex organization.
A professional accounting designation, with strong technical grounding across accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting and internal controls. The underlying profile calls for a CPA/CA-preferred designation and experience with IFRS, ASPE and ASNPO.
Experience leading strong teams through periods of transition, change or transformation
.
A genuinely hands-on style. Someone prepared to get into the numbers and issues rather than lead exclusively from 30,000 feet.
The ability to move comfortably between strategy and execution
.
Exposure to facilities, procurement and broader corporate services would be highly valuable.
Strong executive presence and the ability to establish credibility quickly with senior executives, employees, external advisors and governance stakeholders.
A pragmatic, collaborative leadership style with the confidence to respectfully challenge the status quo.
Experience operating across both mission-driven/not-for-profit and commercially oriented environments
would be particularly attractive.

Why This Assignment?

For the right interim executive, this offers the opportunity to do what great interims do best: step into an important organization at an important moment and make a measurable difference.

You will be joining a high-performing team rather than rebuilding a broken function. The opportunity is to provide leadership through transition, bring an objective external lens, elevate financial and operational practices, and create sustainable improvements that remain long after the assignment has concluded.

This is an assignment for someone who enjoys being more than a caretaker. It requires an executive who can protect what is working, challenge what can be better, and create momentum for what comes next.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an exceptional opportunity for a strategic, government-savvy finance leader to serve as Director of Finance and help shape the fiscal future of the Town of High Level. Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Director of Finance is responsible for the overall leadership and management of the Town’s financial operations. This includes overseeing strategic financial planning, accounting, revenue collection, and cash management, ensuring alignment with the Town’s adopted plans, policies, bylaws, regulations, and standards. In addition to fostering interdepartmental collaboration and ensuring compliance with all financial obligations as outlined in the Municipal Government Act (MGA), the Director supervises a team of four (4): a Financial Analyst, Accounts Payable and Receivable Clerk, Utilities and Tax Clerk, and Support Services Clerk.

THE ORGANIZATION

The Town of High Level is a vibrant northern community of approximately 4,000 residents, serving as the regional service and trading centre for a surrounding population of more than 30,000 people. Located in the northwest corner of Alberta, High Level is strategically positioned at the intersection of Highways 35 and 58, providing critical access to northern industries and communities.

High Level is recognized as a hub for healthcare, education, retail, construction, transportation, and resource development, offering a unique blend of professional challenge and community connection. Known for its breathtaking Northern Lights, endless summer days and access to pristine lakes, rivers and outdoor adventures, the Town is a gateway to exceptional northern living. Residents also enjoy a strong sense of community and rich Indigenous culture, with local festivals, rodeos, and family-oriented activities year-round.

Vision

High Level, an inclusive and vibrant community, with a strong and resilient economy that offers an active and healthy lifestyle.

Mission

We foster a thriving community that enhances our quality of life through sustainable planning, economic prosperity, and inclusion.

For more information, please visit their website: www.highlevel.ca

RESPONSIBILITIES

Plans, directs and coordinates the functions and workload within the Department and ensures that schedules, procedures and performance standards are developed and met.
Utilizes significant judgement, initiative and conceptual thinking in the planning, development and implementation of programs and policies affecting matters related to the scope of duties of this position.
Plans, directs and coordinates the preparation of annual and long-term operational and capital budgets. Provides direct oversight, control and implementation of approved budgets.
Responsible for the preparation of statements and reports on municipal financial affairs for CAO, Directors, Council and the public; includes financial reports on the status and variance of all operating and capital budgets.
Responsible for compiling and supplying information relating to the financial affairs of the municipality as required by Municipal Affairs.
Prepares all financial bylaws, resolutions and subsequent amendments relating to the revenues, expenditures, tax levies and other fiscal and operating matters within the scope of duties of this position. This includes, but is not limited to, bylaws related to the Financial Plan, fees & charges, user rates, tax rates, loan authorization and others.
Administers the provision and management of property insurance policies, claims and related activities.
Oversees the delivery of the Town’s support services, including audit, accounting, taxation, treasury functions, and the management of financial software systems.
Prepares year-end financial working papers, internal statements and municipal reporting forms for audit review and liaises with the Town auditors in connection with the financial audit.
Supports procurement and contract management processes to ensure fiscal responsibility.
Oversees the development and maintenance of the Town’s asset management plan, including strategies, policies and procedures.
Oversees the development of policies for Financial Services. Provides input to policies of other departments.
Provides advice to Town staff, including explanation and interpretation of bylaws, procedures and legislative requirements affecting the Financial Administration department related to the scope of duties of this position.
Responsible for the supervision and mentoring of finance staff including hiring, training, dismissal, appraisals and evaluations of Financial Services employees within approved personnel policies.
Directs, coordinates, and supervises subordinate staff activities and contract staff. Monitors their work performance and delegates work appropriately.
Prepares, or directs the preparation, of reports and makes recommendations to the Chief Administrative Officer on financial matters related to the scope of duties of the position.
Attends all Council meetings, Committee meetings, public hearings and public meetings as required and as directed by the Chief Administrative Officer.
Prepares reports and statistical summaries as necessary for review by the Chief Administrative Officer, Council or other bodies.
As a member of the Senior Management Team, supports and assists other senior managers and is respectful of colleagues' roles, responsibilities and perspectives.
May be required to assist the Town in providing emergency services. Duties assigned during an emergency may differ from regular duties.
Follows and ensures compliance with all policies, procedures, regulations and standards of the Town of High Level.

QUALIFICATIONS

Degree from a recognized post-secondary institution in Accounting, Finance, Business or Public Administration.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation.
Minimum of five (5) years of increasingly responsible, relevant experience in public sector finance (including supervisory experience), preferably in a local government setting, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Thorough and demonstrated knowledge of the principles and practices of public sector accounting standards (PSAS), internal control procedures, computerized financial applications, finance and fiscal planning, and budgetary, accounting and reporting systems.
Thorough and demonstrated knowledge of municipal legislation including the Municipal Government Act and other related regulations, policies and procedures.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Demonstrated knowledge of GAAP, Public Sector Accounting and Budget processes.
Demonstrated leadership skills.
Exceptional interpersonal, communication, presentation, public relations, problem-solving, investigative, decision-making, leadership and general management skills.
Effective written and verbal communication skills including the ability to prepare comprehensive, concise and clear reports and deliver oral presentations.
Ability to multi-task with strong attention to detail.
Results-oriented in a multi-faceted, fast-paced environment with changing priorities.
Knowledge of and demonstrated fiscal responsibility in support of budget preparation and control.
Ability to work effectively, independently and cooperatively in a team atmosphere.
Ability to exercise courtesy, tact, and diplomacy in the exchange of non-routine information with other employees, employees of private companies and members of the general public.
Exceptionally well organized and able to work effectively with minimal guidelines and supervision.
Ability to exercise sound judgement regarding confidential and sensitive information.
Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office applications and extensive knowledge in computer systems relevant to municipal operations. Experience with Questica Budget and Diamond ERP Accounting Software is desired.

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
jobs.description:
Who we are

Kilmer Group is a multi-generational platform for business development and investment, built on operational excellence, long-term stewardship, and trusted relationships. Headquartered in Toronto, we invest across three core sectors: Private Equity, Infrastructure & Real Estate, and Sports & Media, partnering with exceptional management teams to build and grow enduring businesses.

Kilmer Group has built a reputation for disciplined investment, active ownership, and creating long-term value. Our approach is grounded in partnership, integrity, and a commitment to building businesses that generate lasting impact for our partners, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

Who we need

Reporting to the CFO, we are hiring a Vice President, Finance to play a key leadership role across Kilmer Group's finance function. As our new Vice President, Finance, you will combine financial stewardship with strategic partnership, helping guide decisions that support the continued growth and evolution of a diversified investment platform. Working closely with the CFO, senior leaders, and investment teams, you will oversee financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, investment portfolio reporting, and governance while providing the financial insight that supports investment decisions, business performance, and long-term value creation. You will lead a finance team and contribute across a broad range of initiatives, from evaluating acquisitions and investments to strengthening reporting, improving processes, and building the financial capabilities and infrastructure needed to support the organization's continued growth.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, working onsite five days per week.

What’s in it for you?

Strategic influence. Reporting directly to the CFO, you will act as a trusted partner to the executive leadership team, contributing financial insight that informs investment decisions, capital allocation, and the long-term direction of Kilmer Group.

Breadth and exposure. This is an opportunity to apply your expertise across a diverse investment portfolio rather than within a single operating business. You will work on initiatives spanning financial reporting, tax, budgeting, long-term forecasting, governance, and business performance.

Build what's next. Technology and AI are transforming the finance function, and Kilmer Group is evolving with it - strengthening reporting, deepening financial analysis, and modernizing our processes to harness these new tools. You will help build new capabilities, grow a high-performing team, and shape a financial foundation built for long-term success.

As our new VP Finance, you will

Lead the finance function.
You will oversee accounting, treasury, financial reporting, and cash management across a complex, multi-entity organization, ensuring strong controls, effective budgeting, and timely, accurate reporting. As a trusted partner to the CFO, you will provide the financial leadership and operational oversight that enables the team to deliver with confidence while supporting the organization's growth objectives.
Provide strategic financial insight.
You will translate financial information into meaningful analysis that supports executive decision-making. Working closely with the CFO and senior leaders, you will develop reporting and insights that strengthen planning, support investment decisions, and provide a clearer understanding of business performance across the organization.
Support investments and corporate growth.
You will partner with the investment team on acquisitions, portfolio reporting, valuations, due diligence, and other strategic initiatives. You will work closely with leaders across Kilmer Group and its portfolio companies, providing financial guidance and building trusted relationships that support long-term value creation.
Lead and develop the team.
You will mentor, coach, and support the continued growth of the finance team while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and low-ego environment. You will build capability and create opportunities for continuous learning amongst the team.

You bring

The leadership.
You have experience leading high-performing finance teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You are a trusted advisor who can balance strategic priorities with operational execution while building strong relationships across the organization.
The foundation.
You are a CPA, CA with experience gained in both public accounting and industry, ideally including a Big 4 audit environment. You bring strong technical knowledge of ASPE and IFRS, investment holding company accounting, including asset valuations and investee reporting. You have experience with compliance and risk to ensure adherence with tax laws, accounting standards and internal controls. You know how to apply this technical foundation in a commercial environment, combining accounting expertise with sound strategic and business judgment.
The financial expertise.
You bring experience across financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, cash management, tax and corporate governance within complex organizations. You have worked with investment portfolios, valuations, transactions, or corporate development activities and are comfortable partnering with senior leaders to support investment decisions and long-term value creation.
The analytical mindset.
You are naturally curious and continuously look for ways to improve how work gets done. You leverage data and technology to strengthen reporting and decision-making, and you are excited by the opportunity to modernize finance through automation and the thoughtful application of AI.
The communication skills.
You can translate complex financial information into clear recommendations that support decision-making. Whether working with executives, portfolio company leaders, auditors, or external advisors, you build credibility through sound judgment, strong communication, and a collaborative approach.

Why join Kilmer Group?

Today, Kilmer Group continues to build on decades of successful investment and business leadership offering a dynamic and supportive environment with opportunities for growth and development. Beyond our investments, we are committed to strengthening the communities where we live and work through initiatives that support sport, health, research, and community development. Joining Kilmer Group means becoming part of an organization that thinks for the long term, values partnership, and is committed to building a lasting legacy.

Join us

We recognize that no candidate brings every qualification to a role. If your experience is closely aligned with what we are looking for and you are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Kilmer Group, we encourage you to apply. We look forward to learning more about your experience and the perspective you would bring to our team.

What you can expect from our interview process

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining Kilmer Group and your experience. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
An in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to discuss your leadership experience, your approach to building high-performing finance functions, and how you partner with executives to support investment decisions and long-term growth.
An in-person presentation and discussion with the Vice President, Talent and Special Projects and a senior member of the finance team. You will be asked to prepare and present a case study, followed by a conversation about your thinking, priorities, and leadership approach.
A final in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to explore mutual fit, discuss your vision for the role, and answer any remaining questions. Finalists may also have the opportunity to meet additional members of the leadership team.

Kilmer Group is committed to creating a workplace where people are treated with respect, supported in their development, and empowered to contribute their best work. We recognize that diverse perspectives strengthen our business and help us make better decisions for our organization, our partners, and the communities in which we operate.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and are committed to providing an accessible recruitment process. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

The organization manages a diverse portfolio of assets and operates with a long‑term, hands‑on ownership approach, emphasizing financial discipline, operational efficiency, and sustainable growth.

Reporting directly to ownership, the Director of Finance will oversee the full accounting function and play a key role in maintaining the financial health of the organization. jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

RSM Consulting is seeking a Director to serve as Business Transformation Lead on large, integrated Intelligent Finance transformations. Our Intelligent Finance portfolio helps clients build the intelligent foundation and activate AI for Finance at scale — spanning ERP Modernization, Finance Operating Model Transformations, Finance Data & Analytics Modernization and AI Readiness, AI Enablement & Agentic Automation for the Office of Finance as well as Finance Service Delivery Transformations – including centralization, Finance Shared Services and Global Finance Service Delivery.

This is the pivotal business-side leadership role on the transformation. You own how the client operates differently once the platform is live. You are not the program manager and you are not the solution architect — you are the leader accountable for the future-state operating model, the end-to-end processes, the human experience of the change, and the executive confidence that the business, not just the technology, actually changed. Your success is measured by a single question: did the business change successfully?

You will be dedicated to one major transformation at a time, working as a peer alongside the Executive Transformation Partner, the Transformation Director, and the Platform & Delivery Lead.

Responsibilities

Operating Model and Process Ownership
Own the design and operationalization of the future-state operating model for the Finance and Operations functions — finance, supply chain, service, IT, and the shared data and reporting layer that the modernized core creates.
Lead end-to-end business capability and process design across core cycles affected by ERP, Finance point solutions, cloud, data, and AI enablement work, and define how those processes operate in a modernized, increasingly automated environment.
Define the organization, role, skill, decision-rights, and control implications of a modern core and an agentic operating environment — including which decisions become automated, which remain human, and how exceptions are handled and governed.
Establish how data ownership, stewardship, and definitional consistency are carried by the business after the build team leaves.
Maintain traceability from the client’s business case through operating-model changes, process changes, backlog priorities, adoption outcomes, and value delivered.

Human-Centered Design

Own Human-Centered Design as a funded, staffed, and measured workstream from mobilization — not a go-live activity.
Start from user jobs-to-be-done for Finance, rather than screens; ensure personas and journey maps for finance, operations, and service users drive requirements before build.
Prototype and test with real users ahead of build, and use “art-of-the-possible” demonstrations of modern and AI-enabled capability to build executive and user confidence early.
Ensure HCD findings materially shape scope — including where an AI or automation use case is not yet appropriate for the client’s data maturity or risk tolerance.

Organizational Change Management and Adoption

Own OCM as a funded, measured workstream: leader alignment and visible sponsorship from day one, stakeholder analysis, communications, resistance management, role-based training, and readiness scoring.
Baseline adoption targets and tie them explicitly to benefits realization — system usage, process compliance, automation acceptance rates, exception volumes, and reporting adoption.
Lead the business through the behavioral shift that modernization demands: fewer manual reconciliations, more trust in a single data source, and confident supervision of automated and agent-assisted work.

Backlog, Value Mapping and Delivery Cadence

Lead weekly backlog refinement and own product backlog integrity and value mapping — from business drivers through requirements, capabilities, features, adoption outcomes, and measurable benefits.
Participate in each sprint’s feature review and system demonstration alongside the client Product Owner and the Platform & Delivery Lead, assessing whether what was built changes how the business actually works.
Participate in increment planning and Inspect & Adapt retrospectives, testing outcomes against the client’s original drivers.
Ensure outcome milestones are tracked alongside technical and delivery milestones.

Transformation Leadership and Client Confidence

Serve as the bridge between technical delivery and executive confidence, presenting evidence of business change to sponsors, steering committees, and the Executive Risk Committee.
Escalate early, with a recommended action rather than a status — particularly on scope that risks delivering a platform without an operating-model change.
Plan for complexity: competing stakeholder demands, third-party and systems-integrator friction, legacy-process attachment, and key-person risk on both sides.
Bring in-person presence to large or sensitive transformations.

Practice and People Leadership

Contribute to the growth of RSM’s Total Consulting transformation capability, including methods, tools, and reusable intellectual property for operating-model design, HCD, and adoption measurement.
Mentor, coach, and develop managers and senior associates across HCD, process design, and change workstreams
Support pursuits, proposals, and thought leadership that position RSM as a leader in integrated, outcome-led modernization; help shape scope, approach, and change-workstream sizing before mobilization.
Support account expansion through demonstrated value, and maintain strong attention to engagement economics within your workstreams.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
10+ years of consulting or advisory experience, including significant experience leading business-side transformation on large enterprise technology programs.
Demonstrated ownership of the Finance future-state operating model and end-to-end process design on ERP, cloud, data, or AI-enabled programs.
Demonstrated ownership of change and adoption as a funded workstream, including baselined adoption targets tied to benefits.
Experience operating in a fixed Agile or scaled-Agile cadence, including product backlog ownership, backlog refinement, and sprint demonstrations with an active client Product Owner.
Strong executive presence and the ability to hold candid, evidence-based conversations with C-suite sponsors.
Practical understanding of modern ERP, cloud, data, and AI platform capability — sufficient to shape requirements and challenge design, without acting as the technical architect.
Commitment to responsible AI use with a human in the loop and human accountability for all client-facing judgments and outputs.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, generally up to 50%, with in-person presence on large programs.

Preferred Qualifications

CPA and / or Masters in Business Administration, with a focus on Accounting, Finance or Operations
Experience on transformations where an implementation was deliberately converted into a program as scope expanded across process, organization, and adoption.
Experience designing operating models for finance, supply chain, or shared-services functions in a modernized core environment.
Experience establishing AI and automation governance from a business-process and control perspective.
Change certification such as Prosci/ADKAR; design-thinking or service-design credentials; SAFe Agilist, PMI-ACP, or Scrum Master certification

jobs.title: Director, Canada Strategy
jobs.description:
At Manulife Canada, the Strategy & Transformation team sits at the center of the organization, partnering closely with the Canada CEO and Segment leaders to shape and advance the company’s long-term direction.

We work across business lines and functions to translate Segment strategy into aligned priorities, maintain an integrated view of the strategic portfolio, shape high-impact initiatives, and improve the processes through which strategic and investment decisions are made.

As Director, Canada Strategy, you will help shape Manulife Canada’s strategy and advance its most critical priorities. You will combine enterprise perspective, structured problem solving, and constructive challenge to help senior leaders make clear choices and mobilize action.

This high-visibility role spans strategy reviews, strategic initiatives, and business and functional deep dives. The Director will act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders and help connect Canada Segment priorities with business unit and functional plans.

This role is ideal for a strategy leader who has shaped enterprise or business-unit strategy in a complex organization or top-tier consulting environment and is equally comfortable developing strategy, facilitating executive decisions, and moving priority initiatives toward execution.

Position Responsibilities

Strategy Cascade and Enterprise Visibility

Translate Canada Segment strategy into clear priorities, expectations, and decision criteria for business units and functions.
Lead periodic strategy reviews and structured check-ins to assess progress, test whether priorities remain valid, and identify where leadership intervention is required.
Maintain an integrated view of the strategic portfolio, including both funded initiatives and material work outside the formal book of work, to identify gaps, overlaps, dependencies, and emerging risks.
Synthesize business unit and functional strategies to assess how they collectively advance Canada Segment objectives.
Help develop and communicate the narrative of the Canada Segment strategy to Enterprise leadership and the Board.

Strategic Initiatives and Enterprise Problem Solving

Lead high-priority, cross-business strategic initiatives from problem definition through recommendation, mobilization, and transition to accountable execution owners.
Frame and evaluate strategic choices, including where to enter, exit, invest, partner, acquire, simplify, or double down.
Develop fact-based recommendations through structured problem solving, market and competitive analysis, financial assessment, scenario analysis, and stakeholder input.
Develop business cases and implementation roadmaps, establish intended outcomes and success measures, and secure senior leadership alignment.
Support partnership and M&A assessments, including strategic fit, value creation logic, key risks, and integration considerations, in collaboration with relevant subject-matter experts.

Business and Functional Deep Dives

Lead periodic vertical and horizontal deep dives across businesses and functions, for example – Distribution, Technology, Operations, and other enterprise capabilities.
Act as the Canada Segment’s thought and challenge partner to functions, testing strategic ambition, investment priorities, operating choices, and alignment with business needs.
Identify cross-business opportunities, shared capabilities, and structural barriers that may not be visible within individual portfolios.
Facilitate alignment across business and functional leaders where priorities, accountabilities, or investment choices are unclear.

Executive Advisory and Team Leadership

Provide independent, forward-looking advice to senior executives and facilitate decisions on complex or ambiguous strategic topics.
Develop concise executive and Board-ready materials that clarify the issue, choices, trade-offs, recommendation, and required decision.
Build alignment across business units, functions, and enterprise partners through effective facilitation, influence, and constructive challenge.
Lead and develop a high-performing, inclusive team with strong capabilities in strategic judgment, structured problem solving, executive communication, and delivery.
Coach direct reports and peers, allocate resources to the highest-value priorities
Strengthen the Strategy & Transformation team’s methods and capabilities – including via the adoption of AI, better operating rhythms, common approaches, etc.

Leadership Capabilities

Strategic Judgment: Connect enterprise context, market evidence, economics, and execution realities to make clear recommendations.
Structured Problem Solving: Break ambiguous issues into testable hypotheses, focused analyses, and practical choices.
Influence and Constructive Challenge: Build credibility with senior leaders while testing assumptions and surfacing trade-offs.
Executive Communication: Distill complex issues into concise, decision-oriented narratives and Board-ready materials.
Enterprise Collaboration: Create alignment across business units and functions without relying on formal authority.
Mobilization and Execution: Translate strategy into clear outcomes, accountabilities, success measures, and an executable path forward.
Talent Development: Coach and develop high-performing strategy talent and raise the quality of thinking across the team.

Required Qualifications

8–10+ years of progressively senior experience in corporate strategy, business strategy, management consulting, corporate development, transformation, or a related field.
Experience in financial services and/or a top-tier consulting firm strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience shaping enterprise or business-unit strategy across multiple businesses, functions, or geographies.
Strong financial acumen, including experience developing business cases, assessing investment choices, and evaluating value creation and risk.
Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems, develop and test hypotheses, synthesize quantitative and qualitative evidence, and translate analysis into practical recommendations.
Strong track record of influencing senior stakeholders, facilitating difficult decisions, and delivering measurable outcomes in complex, matrixed environments.
Experience with strategic planning, portfolio prioritization, operating model assessment, transformation, and benefits realization.
People leadership experience, including coaching and developing high-performing teams.
University degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field.
MBA, equivalent graduate degree, or relevant professional designation preferred.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

new_jobs.description:
The Company

Cover Genius is the global infrastructure for embedded protection. Active in over 60 countries and all 50 US States, we protect the customers of the world’s largest digital companies, including Klarna, Revolut, Stripe, Priceline, Agoda, Booking.com, Turkish Airlines, Tongcheng Travel, eBay, and Uber, with seamless, end-to-end experiences. Cover Genius has protected more than 73M customers globally across 240M policies with USD $3.2BN in gross written sales.

Coming off a stellar year with 40% YoY revenue growth and a recent $100M capital raise, putting our valuation at $1.9BN, we are accelerating into our next phase of growth. As part of our team, you’ll help drive our AI-first roadmap, developing hyper-personalization engines, agentic distribution, and automated claims infrastructure, while building the scalable technology powering the fast-growing $70B embedded protection market.

Our people are:
Accountable, customer-obsessed, collaborative, driven

Our people are not:
Passive, defensive, siloed, hesitant

About The Role

As Senior Director of Data on our Technology team, you will own Cover Genius' data strategy end-to-end and act as domain lead for Data Products, accountable for its OKRs, roadmap, and delivery. You will work closely with our partnership teams to understand what partners need to see, and give them a clear view of how their insurance business is performing.

To drive success in this role, you will bring a genuine blend of commercial instinct, product judgement, and deep technical credibility — the breadth to lead a business domain, not just an engineering function. You will be as effective influencing at exec level, ours and our partners', as you are leading the engineers and analysts who report to you. Close collaboration with Engineering, Product, Data Science, Analytics, and our own commercial and partner-facing teams will be central to the role — ensuring data becomes a trusted, reusable foundation every other domain can build on with confidence. You will treat AI as a first-class concern of the role — building a platform that AI workloads can trust, exploring AI-enhanced partner propositions, and driving AI-assisted ways of working within your own org.

Key Responsibilities

Work closely with our commercial and partner-facing teams to understand what partners actually need and want from our data, and help shape that into offers they find compelling.
Set product direction for internal and partner-facing data products, partnering with the executive and senior leadership teams to define OKRs and roadmap, and own their execution.
Own the data platform strategy and architecture end-to-end, ensuring it keeps pace as our data grows in volume, velocity, and variety — including the data foundations that AI/ML workloads across the business depend on.
Drive adoption of the data platform across business domains, so Engineering, Data, and Product teams build their solutions on a shared data foundation.
Build governance and data-quality frameworks that make our key data assets trustworthy.
Develop a high-performing Data organisation where people love their work and grow into future leaders.

What You Will Bring

12+ years in data roles spanning platform, product and B2B partner-facing work, including 5+ years leading teams of managers and senior contributors — ideally in a regulated, high-growth B2B business.
You are comfortable working alongside commercial and partner-facing teams, can hold your own in a partner conversation, and have a track record of translating what customers want into propositions that land.
You have owned a roadmap, made hard prioritisation calls between platform investment and customer-facing delivery, and can explain the calls you got wrong.
Strong record of partnering with Engineering, Product, Data Science, Analytics and other data consumers to turn data into a trusted, reusable foundation.
Deep, hands-on architecture credibility on a modern cloud data stack — ideally GCP/BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, and data observability tooling, including experience building and operating data platforms that serve AI/ML workloads.
Proven record of establishing governance and data-quality frameworks that enable delivery rather than block it, and that are adopted across large data-centric organisations.
Practical fluency in data security and privacy in a regulated context such as insurance or financial services.

What You Will Have

Bias for action — you ship incremental improvements continuously rather than waiting for perfect conditions, act decisively, and hold a high bar for what "done" means.
Ownership without excuses — you take personal accountability for team outcomes, including the misses and talk about failures as candidly as wins.
Growth mindset — you share knowledge generously, learn from setbacks and have a track record of developing engineers and managers who go on to bigger roles.
Influence over authority — you push teams to think bigger and drive adoption of standards through credibility and clear reasoning, not mandate.
Partner and customer obsession — you're truly curious about Cover Genius' partners and trace every decision back to the customer experience or partner outcome it improves.

🤔 Why Cover Genius?

At Cover Genius, We Create Magic By Turning The Archaic Into The Extraordinary. We Take One Of The World’s Oldest And Most Complex Industries And Reinvent It With World-class Technology. Cover Genius Doesn’t Just Disrupt Legacy Insurance; We Make The Impossible Feel Effortless. Our Operating Principles Guide Our Mission

Make today matter: We deliver with urgency and excellence. We act decisively, move with intention, and hold a high bar.
Act with accountability: We own our commitments and take pride in delivering results that move us forward.
Grow together: We are a collective of curious minds. We learn from wins and setbacks, share knowledge generously, and elevate each other every day.
Inspire Each Other: We push each other to think bigger and pull together to go further.
Champion Our Customers: We lead with empathy and center the customer, turning complex disruptions into seamless moments of trust.
Flexible Work Environment - Our teams are hybrid. We work from home on a Wednesday and Thursday and attend the office on Monday, Tuesday and Friday with flexibility around start/finish times.
Don't just take our word for it - hear about our culture straight from our people here: story time.

Ready to make an impact?
If you’re looking for a place where you’ll be challenged, trusted, and empowered, we’d love to meet you.

The Legal & Privacy Stuff

Cover Genius promotes diversity and inclusivity. We don't tolerate discrimination, demeaning treatment of anyone, or harassment due to race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or any other legally protected status.

new_jobs.description:
This role is HYBRID, requires senior leadership and hands on capability to build complex AI solutions.

About the role:

BMO Canada Wealth Digital is accelerating the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across its customer-facing digital platforms to enhance client experiences, improve operational efficiency, and enable innovative wealth management solutions. We are seeking an experienced AI Delivery Director to lead the planning, execution, and delivery of strategic AI initiatives that support the evolution of our Wealth Management digital capabilities.

This is a senior delivery leadership role requiring the coordination of cross-functional teams across Engineering, Architecture, Security, Risk Management, Compliance, and Business organizations. The successful candidate will be responsible for driving the delivery of secure, compliant, and resilient Multi-Agent AI solutions that leverage enterprise AI capabilities, including the AI Gateway, Policy Engine, Identity Fabric, AI Registry, Guardrails Runtime, Model Context Protocol (MCP) services, and AI Observability platforms.

The AI Delivery Director will provide end-to-end leadership across the delivery lifecycle, from intake, discovery, and prioritization through implementation, deployment, adoption, and business value realization by adopting and utilizing AI tools in SDLC. Working closely with engineering leaders, product owners, architects, and executive stakeholders, the role will ensure AI-enabled solutions are delivered on schedule, aligned with enterprise standards, and integrated effectively within the broader technology ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Technology Delivery
Lead delivery across multiple cross-functional product and platform teams, establishing one integrated plan, clear critical path, transparent dependencies, and accountable owners.
Convert the product roadmap into executable technology increments, release plans, capacity models, milestones, and outcome-based commitments.
Drive delivery discipline across scope, schedule, cost, quality, resources, risk, and benefits, using forecasts rather than artificial certainty.
Identify constraints early, remove impediments, resolve cross-team trade-offs, and escalate decisions with clear options and recommendations.
Ensure each release has explicit entry, exit, acceptance, operational readiness, and rollback criteria.
AI Engineering and AI SDLC Leadership
Apply deep knowledge of generative AI and agentic systems, including LLM orchestration, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt and context engineering, evaluations, guardrails, memory, and human oversight.
Embed full-lifecycle AI SDLC practices across requirements, design, build, test, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and model or prompt change management.
Ensure AI quality is measured using fit-for-purpose evaluations covering safety, groundedness, relevance, accuracy, latency, reliability, and client experience.
Champion specification-driven development, automation, reusable engineering patterns, and AI-assisted software delivery where approved.
Ensure deterministic software testing and probabilistic AI evaluation are integrated into CI/CD and release decisions.
Azure, Architecture and Platform Integration
Provide senior technical leadership for solutions deployed on Microsoft Azure and integrated with BMO InvestorLine and Wealth Management platforms.
Partner with solution, enterprise, security, data, and platform architects to maintain an approved, scalable target architecture and prevent local optimization or avoidable technical debt.
Ensure APIs, event flows, data services, identity, access, observability, resilience, and non-functional requirements are designed and delivered end to end.
Drive environment readiness, infrastructure as code, automated deployment, telemetry, performance engineering, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and production support readiness.
Promote reuse of enterprise AI capabilities, shared services, patterns, and controls while preserving clear service boundaries and ownership.
Advanced Agile and Value-Stream Delivery
Establish and continuously improve an advanced Agile operating model organized around persistent, cross-functional teams and measurable client or business outcomes.
Lead portfolio and product-level planning, backlog readiness, dependency management, release forecasting, and flow optimization across multiple teams.
Use evidence-based metrics such as lead time, cycle time, throughput, work in progress, predictability, escaped defects, reliability, evaluation performance, and value realization.
Reduce handoffs, unnecessary governance, meeting load, and blocked work; create fast decision paths and clear single-point accountability.
Coach delivery leaders, Scrum Masters, engineering leads, and teams in modern product delivery, DevSecOps, continuous delivery, and learning-driven retrospectives.
Quality, Risk and Responsible AI
Build quality, privacy, security, regulatory compliance, model risk, accessibility, and responsible AI requirements into delivery from inception, not as release-end checkpoints.
Partner with Legal, Risk, Compliance, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Model Risk, Data Governance, and Technology Risk to establish proportionate controls and auditable evidence.
Ensure full-spectrum observability across application, infrastructure, data, model, prompt, agent, safety, and client-experience performance.
Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and learning reviews for technology or AI quality events.
Maintain transparent risk, issue, dependency, and decision records and ensure material risks are escalated promptly.
Stakeholder, Financial and Partner Leadership
Serve as the senior technology delivery voice for Em with InvestorLine, Wealth, Technology & Operations, Applied AI, governance partners, and executive forums.
Provide concise, fact-based reporting on outcomes, delivery confidence, risks, financials, quality, and decisions required.
Own technology delivery financial stewardship, resource planning, vendor performance, commercial dependencies, and delivery commitments.
Lead co-build and vendor engagements with clear accountability, knowledge transfer, architecture compliance, security obligations, and measurable outcomes.
Create an inclusive, high-accountability environment that develops leaders, strengthens technical depth, and keeps teams focused on client outcomes.

Key Success Measures

Predictable delivery of roadmap outcomes and releases, with transparent forecast accuracy and controlled scope change.
Measurable improvement in delivery flow, engineering productivity, automation, quality, and time to value.
AI evaluation thresholds and non-functional requirements met before release and sustained in production.
Stable, secure, resilient production performance with effective observability, incident management, and continuous improvement.
Clear ownership, faster decisions, fewer cross-team handoffs, and effective dependency resolution.
Measurable client adoption, experience, business value, and risk outcomes delivered in partnership with the Product Owner.
Effective financial, capacity, vendor, and technical-debt management.

Required Skills And Competencies

Expert-level technology delivery leadership in large, complex, regulated environments, with accountability for multiple teams and production outcomes.
Deep practical knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI delivery, including agentic architectures, LLM application patterns, evaluations, guardrails, observability, and responsible AI controls.
Strong knowledge of wealth management and digital investing platforms, including client journeys, advice or guidance experiences, market and portfolio data, trading-related integrations, and regulatory considerations.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Azure cloud architecture and delivery, cloud-native engineering, APIs, integration, identity and access, data services, telemetry, resilience, and DevSecOps.
Mastery of advanced Agile, product operating models, value-stream management, Lean flow, Scrum or Kanban, portfolio planning, CI/CD, test automation, and evidence-based delivery metrics.
Ability to challenge constructively, make decisions under ambiguity, translate technical complexity into business implications, and influence senior executives.
Commercial and financial acumen, including technology investment, capacity, vendor, contract, and delivery-performance management.
Exceptional leadership, communication, facilitation, negotiation, and talent-development skills.

Qualifications And Experience

15+ years of progressive experience in technology delivery, engineering, architecture, platform, or product technology leadership, including senior leadership accountability.
Demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale digital products or platforms from strategy through production and ongoing operation.
Demonstrated delivery of AI/ML or generative AI solutions in production, ideally involving multi-agent systems or other complex AI-enabled client experiences.
Significant experience with Microsoft Azure and modern software engineering practices in a regulated enterprise.
Experience in wealth management, brokerage, digital investing, banking, or similarly regulated financial services is strongly preferred.
Proven experience leading cross-functional internal and partner teams through complex dependencies and high-stakes releases.
University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business, or a related discipline; relevant advanced degree or certifications are considered assets.
Experience in Wealth Management or Capital Markets AI space (highly desirable) or Financial Institutions or Technology firms.
Domain knowledge of investment, securities, trading from a technology perspective, having worked in such ecosystems.

Leadership Expectations

Act as an owner: accountable for outcomes, not activity or coordination alone.
Put clients, safety, quality, and sustainable value ahead of pace without evidence.
Create clarity: make responsibilities, decisions, risks, dependencies, and delivery confidence visible.
Lead with technical credibility while empowering engineering and product leaders closest to the work.
Build trust through candor, transparency, inclusion, disciplined follow-through, and continuous learning.

new_jobs.title: Director, Data Foundations, Automation & Infrastructure
new_jobs.description:
About the Opportunity:

This is an exciting leadership opportunity within Commercial Banking to shape the future of how data powers business decisions across Canada and the U.S.

As Director, Data Foundations, Automation & Information Infrastructure, you will lead a highly technical team responsible for delivering trusted, curated, and scalable data assets that support reporting, analytics, AI, and strategic decision-making across Commercial Banking. You will oversee data engineering, data operations, information infrastructure, and business-managed applications while influencing the broader Commercial Banking data strategy.

The role combines banking knowledge, technical leadership, people management, and strategic thinking. As the organization continues its journey toward cloud modernization, AI-enabled automation, Client 360 capabilities, and near real-time data delivery, this leader will play a critical role in shaping the future state of Commercial Banking's data ecosystem.

This opportunity is ideal for a banking-savvy technology leader who enjoys building high-performing teams, solving complex data challenges, driving modernization initiatives, and translating business needs into scalable technical solutions.

About This Role

The Director, Data Foundations leads the team responsible for building, managing and continuously improving the curated data that powers Commercial Banking. This includes client, financial, client activity and master data, along with the other key business data sets that reporting, analytics and AI teams across the organization rely on to make decisions.

The Director owns the end-to-end data lifecycle, from requirements, data modeling and architecture, through ETL and pipeline development, to the reliable production of trusted data within established service levels. The role partners with business, analytics, AI, Technology and Data Governance partners to ensure data is accurate, well documented and easy to use, and leads the ongoing modernization of data platforms and practices.

The ideal candidate combines deep data management expertise with strong people leadership and a high standard for quality.

Why This Role Matters

Trusted, well-managed data is the foundation for sound decisions, effective and trusted reporting, and the responsible use of AI. This role directly contributes to:

Consistent, reliable data that supports executive reporting and business decision-making
Curated data assets that allow reporting, analytics and AI teams to focus on insights
A scalable, modern data ecosystem that keeps pace with evolving business needs
Strong data quality and control practices aligned to BMO’s data governance standards

Key Responsibilities

Data Strategy and Architecture

Define and deliver the Data Foundations strategy and roadmap, aligned to business, CDAO and enterprise data priorities
Design and maintain the data architecture and models for curated data assets, including master and reference data, with long-term usability and scalability in mind
Establish and uphold standards for data modeling, naming, metadata, integration and data sharing

Data Development and Operations

Lead the design, development and operation of ETL processes and data pipelines
Ensure recurring data production is accurate, timely and reconciled to authoritative sources, within published service levels
Monitor data flows, resolve issues promptly and drive root-cause remediation
Embed data quality checks, validation and controls throughout the data lifecycle
Ensure data is handled securely and protected from loss or unauthorized access, in line with legal and company standards

Modernization and Innovation

Continuously evaluate and adopt technologies, tools and practices that improve the scalability, efficiency and resilience of the data ecosystem
Partner with Technology on platform strategy, infrastructure and the path to production
Prepare and structure data to support advanced analytics and AI use cases

Data Enablement and Partnership

Manage the intake and prioritization of data requests transparently, with clear service levels
Promote data literacy and self-service through documentation, data dictionaries and a community of practice
Serve as a trusted partner to business, analytics, AI and Technology teams on data definitions, changes and their downstream impacts
Partner with Data Governance to meet data quality, metadata, lineage and data risk requirements

Business-Managed Applications

Oversee a portfolio of business-managed applications that support key business processes, from intake and design through delivery, enhancement and ongoing support
Ensure these applications are well controlled and supported, and aligned to BMO technology, data and risk standards

People Leadership

Build, develop and lead a high-performing team of data professionals, working effectively with vendor partners
Set clear goals and accountability, coach for growth, and foster a culture of ownership, quality and continuous improvement
Attract, retain and develop top talent, recognizing strong performance and addressing gaps
Role model BMO values and foster an inclusive culture connected to our purpose
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Who You Are

Treats data as a product: curated, documented, reconciled and reusable
Holds a high standard for accuracy and builds processes that make quality repeatable
Balances stability with progress, modernizing while keeping production dependable
Understands Commercial Banking and how data flows across clients, products and channels
Communicates clearly and builds trust through transparency
Influences without authority and aligns diverse stakeholders around shared definitions
Thrives in ambiguity and brings creative solutions to complex, interdependent problems

9+ years of experience in data management, data engineering or a related field, including leadership of data teams

new_jobs.description:
Your Opportunity at ARC’TERYX:

As the Vice President, Global Consumer Data & Insights, you are a trusted advisor and strategic partner to the Brand Leadership team and to the Enterprise organization, shaping the future of the Arc’teryx brand through deep consumer understanding and insight-led strategy. You will define and lead the company’s Consumer Insights vision, ensuring the voice of the consumer is embedded at the core of brand and business strategy, decision making and long-term growth.  In this role you influence critical business and brand decisions through compelling storytelling and foresight, translating complex data into clear direction for senior leaders.

Acting as a catalyst for a consumer-first culture, you lead the growth of the company’s insights capabilities, operating models, and tools while building a high-performing global team. You also champion innovation in how the organization anticipates and responds to shifting consumer behaviors, ensuring the brand remains culturally relevant and positioned for sustained growth.

Ideally this role is based out of our North Vancouver office.

Meet Your Future Team:

The Brand team is the direct connection between the guest and the core intention of the Arc’teryx brand. Leveraging an increasingly robust set of consumer insights, we specialize in storytelling and creating incredible experiences that connect people to the transformative power of the mountains. Our functions include enterprise strategy, brand marketing and creative, athletes/ambassador's programs, community, experiences, operations, communications, regional teams, and agency partners. This team is comprised of global HQ and regional offices who aim to become the voice of the consumer within the organization.  You will work in close partnership with functional leaders across channels and regions to bring added value to the business during this high growth era.

You and your team will also support wider executive leadership, aggregating data from commercial, product and business partners to derive insights that inform the enterprise growth strategy.

If you were in the VP, Global Consumer Data & Insights role now, here are some of the core activities you would be doing:

Setting the strategic vision and multi-year roadmap for the global Consumer Insights function, strengthening brand equity, distinctiveness, and consumer connection while ensuring alignment to brand positioning, growth priorities, and long-term strategy

Serving as the enterprise leader and trusted advisor for consumer insights, embedding a consumer-first operating model and insight-led perspectives that shape executive decisions, strategic planning, and innovation across all functions, regions, and business units.

Building, leading, and developing a high-performing global Consumer Insights team, including organizational design, capability building, and succession planning

Translating complex, multi-source data into clear narratives and lead the evolution of advanced analytics, including predictive, prescriptive, and AI-driven approaches, next-gen measurement, and marketing effectiveness/ROI tools, to drive measurable business outcomes

Designing and scaling a global insights operating model and enterprise frameworks — tools, platforms, KPIs, and standardized methodologies — and build strategic external partnerships (agencies, data providers, industry experts) to democratize access and ensure best-in-class capability

Leading consumer segmentation and consolidate data and insights systems across the enterprise (with focus on product, channel, and regional data), anticipating emerging consumer behaviors and market dynamics to unlock acquisition, retention, and growth opportunities

Shaping the future of brand-building through next-generation insights, leveraging AI, real-time consumer signals, and emerging technologies to create more adaptive, responsive, and culturally relevant brand strategies

Pioneering new approaches to understanding consumer connection and brand experience, evolving beyond traditional research to integrate behavioral, emotional, and cultural intelligence at scale

Future-proofing the Brand by embedding predictive foresight and scenario planning, enabling the organization to anticipate disruption, stay ahead of shifting consumer expectations, and unlock long-term brand growth opportunities
