ICES is a world-leading health research and analytics institute. With a wealth of data and analytic expertise, we create trusted evidence that has changed health policy and practice and helps ensure better health for all.

Ready to discover more with us? Join our outstanding, collaborative team where your skills, knowledge and curiosity are valued and can change the future of health care.

At ICES, we recognize what matters most to our employees. Some of the great benefits of working at ICES include:

Flexible work arrangements
Competitive Compensation
Comprehensive Benefits Program
HOOPP Pension Plan (Defined Pension)
Employee Assistance Program and Dialogue Well Being Program
Generous vacation, float and caregiver days for all employees
Education Fund and Dedicated Education Days
Holiday Closure
Perkopolis Employee Discount Program

Introduction:

ICES is seeking a Director, Indigenous Partnerships, Data and Analytic Services to join our Indigenous Partnerships, Data and Analytic Services (IPDA) department. Reporting to the Senior Director, Strategic Partnerships and Digital Services, the Director, in collaboration with ICES leadership, is responsible for the development and delivery of the work of the department at ICES. This includes the developing partnerships, guiding governance, connecting with communities, and developing mutual capacity building with First Nations, Métis, Inuit organizational and health service provider partners across urban, rural, and remote geographies

Responsibilities of the position include, but may not be limited to:

Indigenous Partnership Development:

Accountable for developing, implementing, and managing the Indigenous Partnerships, Data and Analytics (IPDA) department at ICES. This includes facilitating the assertion of representative and diverse First Nations, Inuit, and Métis approaches, perspectives, protocols, and practices to leadership at ICES.
Effectively manage all aspects of performance management for direct reports, including coaching individuals and conducting continuous evaluations to enhance team effectiveness and alignment with departmental goals.
Utilize leadership and project management skills to ensure that departmental initiatives align with ICES' strategic objectives and community needs.

Strategy Management and Operational Planning:

Manage the design and development of an effective and ongoing strategy related to Indigenous data and partnerships. This involves advancing the harmonization of ongoing ICES scientific and corporate strategies with First Nations, Inuit, and Métis requirements and protocols.
Employ analytical and strategic planning skills to assess current practices and develop actionable plans. This includes utilizing data analysis tools and stakeholder feedback to inform strategy development and ensure alignment with community needs and organizational objectives.
Work with cross-functional teams to ensure that the strategy is responsive to evolving Indigenous data sovereignty principles, leveraging collaborative skills to engage stakeholders in the process.
Oversee departmental expenses and recovery of costs by reviewing financial reports and tracking operational expenditures and ensure budget compliance.
Analyze budget requirements and make recommendations for resource allocation, ensuring that financial resources are used efficiently to support research projects and departmental initiatives.

Policy Advisory:

Advise on adapting ICES policies and processes to align with the visions, principles, and requirements of First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples across Ontario. This ensures that all organizational practices are culturally relevant and compliant with community expectations.
Utilize knowledge of Indigenous governance and policy frameworks to facilitate discussions with stakeholders, gathering insights and recommendations for policy adaptation. This involves conducting research and engaging with community leaders to ensure that ICES practices reflect Indigenous perspectives and values.
Prepare policy briefs and reports to communicate recommendations to ICES leadership, ensuring that information is clear and actionable.

Education and Capacity Building:

Educate and provide expertise to internal and external partners regarding First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples' data and data use at ICES. This includes developing training materials and conducting workshops to enhance understanding of Indigenous data sovereignty principles.
Leverage communication and presentation skills to effectively convey complex information, utilizing multimedia tools and resources to engage diverse audiences.
Oversee the development of internal and external capacity-building initiatives, collaborating with educational institutions and community organizations to strengthen partnerships and enhance data literacy.

External Representation:

Represent ICES at external meetings and share ICES’ approach to integrating Indigenous data sovereignty principles. This involves engaging with Indigenous thought leaders to seek guidance on best practices and emerging trends in Indigenous data management.
Utilize networking and relationship-building skills to establish and maintain connections with key external stakeholders, ensuring that ICES remains responsive to community needs and perspectives.
Develop proposals and oversee reporting documents for funders and stakeholders

Team Management and Development:

Manage, coach, and evaluate the team by providing regular feedback and facilitating team-building activities to promote collaboration and alignment with goals, utilizing performance management tools and techniques.
Foster a culture of continuous improvement by identifying training needs, organizing professional development opportunities, and mentoring team members to enhance their skills and career growth, ensuring access to relevant resources and training programs.
Utilize leadership and mentoring skills to enhance departmental effectiveness and individual growth, ensuring alignment with ICES' mission and values by creating an inclusive and supportive team environment.

Other:

Other duties as may be assigned within the scope of this position.

Knowledge, skills, and abilities:

Minimum Required Education, Years of Experience:

Bachelor’s Degree in related field;
At least 8 years of Indigenous community and/or research experience;
Experience working with major health system and Indigenous stakeholders and leaders within Ontario;
A minimum of 5 years management experience;
Demonstrated knowledge of Indigenous cultures and histories in Canada.

Preferred Education, Years of Experience:

Master’s degree in related field.;
Demonstrated knowledge of Indigenous cultures and histories in Canada, through personal lived experiences.

Minimum Required Position-Specific Knowledge and Technical Skills:

Understanding and experience working with principles of Indigenous data sovereignty.
Familiarity and knowledge of the diversity of First Nation, Inuit, and Métis Peoples.
Recognized leadership in First Nations, Métis, and/or Inuit communities, demonstrating a commitment to cultural competence and community engagement.
Experience working with Provincial, Territorial and/or Federal government and government agencies;
Demonstrated understanding of Indigenous research methodologies and approaches, with an asset being knowledge of quantitative Indigenous health research methodologies.
Demonstrated understanding of strategic planning and program implementation, ensuring alignment with community needs and organizational goals.
Demonstrated project management expertise, including budget and timeline management, to ensure successful delivery of initiatives.
Demonstrated understanding of the health care system, policy development, and planning in Ontario, particularly as it relates to Indigenous health.
Collaborative leadership skills, demonstrating the ability to lead effective teams toward desired outcomes.

Preferred Position-Specific Knowledge and Technical Skills:

Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly and effectively to diverse audiences.
Relationship building skills, with a proven ability to foster trust and collaboration among stakeholders.
Flexibility and adaptability to work on multiple projects simultaneously, managing competing priorities effectively.
Demonstrated strategic planning and management skills, with a focus on achieving measurable results and community impact.
Knowledge of ICES mission and goals, ensuring that partnerships align with organizational objectives.

This full-time opportunity is for an existing vacancy at ICES Central. The annual salary range for this role is $140,000 - $155,000.

.

À titre de Directeur du programme PRE, vous serez responsable de la gouvernance et de l’exécution de bout en bout de l’écosystème ERP d’IPEX, avec une responsabilité particulière à l’égard du programme de transformation SAP S/4HANA. En étroite collaboration avec les dirigeants des secteurs d’affaires et des technologies de l’information, vous assurerez la réalisation d’une initiative stratégique d’envergure visant à soutenir les objectifs opérationnels et la croissance à long terme de l’entreprise.

Cette fonction représente une occasion unique de jouer un rôle de premier plan au sein de l’un des plus importants programmes de transformation technologique et organisationnelle d’IPEX. À la croisée des technologies, des opérations et de la gouvernance d’entreprise, vous veillerez à l’alignement des priorités d’affaires avec l’exécution du programme à l’échelle de notre réseau manufacturier nord-américain. La personne retenue possède une expertise approfondie de SAP, une solide expérience en gouvernance de programmes et la capacité de piloter des initiatives complexes dans un environnement en constante évolution.

Responsabilités principales

Assurer le succès du programme grâce à un partenariat tripartite structuré entre les TI, les unités d’affaires et l’intégrateur de systèmes, en définissant clairement les rôles, les droits décisionnels et les responsabilités à tous les niveaux de gouvernance.

Établir et appliquer les cadres de gouvernance du programme, incluant les points de contrôle, les comités de pilotage, les registres de risques et les mécanismes d’escalade.
Gérer les calendriers intégrés du programme, les plans de ressources, les risques, les interdépendances et les budgets excédant 10 M$.
Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires composées de plus de 50 employés internes et consultants externes.

Piloter les stratégies de préparation organisationnelle, de gestion du changement et de communication en partenariat avec les équipes responsables de la transformation et des affaires chez IPEX.
Promouvoir la standardisation des processus, la gouvernance des données et la gestion des données maîtres à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

Qualifications Et Expérience

Plus de 10 ans d’expérience progressive en leadership dans le domaine des technologies de l’information, dont un minimum de 5 ans dans des fonctions de direction associées à la livraison de programmes ERP.
Baccalauréat en technologies de l’information, en informatique, en génie ou en administration des affaires (obligatoire); MBA fortement souhaité.
Expérience éprouvée dans la conduite d’implantations complètes de SAP S/4HANA (greenfield ou brownfield) au sein d’environnements manufacturiers ou industriels.
Expérience de gestion de programmes ERP pluriannuels comportant des budgets supérieurs à 10 M$ et des équipes de plus de 50 personnes réparties sur plusieurs sites et plusieurs pays.
Excellente connaissance des modules SAP S/4HANA; familiarité avec SAP BTP ainsi qu’avec la gestion des versions et des environnements SAP.
Excellentes compétences en communication exécutive et capacité à vulgariser des concepts techniques complexes auprès de la haute direction et du conseil d’administration.
Solides aptitudes en négociation, en gestion de fournisseurs et en influence au sein d’environnements matriciels.
Capacité démontrée à évoluer dans l’ambiguïté, à prendre des décisions sous pression et à instaurer un climat de confiance auprès d’équipes multidisciplinaires.
Aptitude à diriger des transformations organisationnelles d’envergure en favorisant l’adhésion, l’alignement et l’engagement des parties prenantes.
Expérience démontrée dans l’atteinte des résultats convenus, la réalisation des bénéfices escomptés, l’amélioration de la performance opérationnelle et l’atteinte des objectifs du programme.
Capacité à identifier, évaluer et atténuer les risques de façon proactive tout en assurant l’efficacité des mécanismes de gouvernance et d’escalade.
Engagement envers l’innovation, l’optimisation des processus et l’excellence opérationnelle afin de maximiser la valeur d’affaires et les capacités de la plateforme ERP.

As the Director of Commercial Pricing and Data Governance at UNFI, you are responsible for developing and executing the company's enterprise-wide pricing strategy while leading the Data Governance function. In the area of pricing, your scope includes building and leading a centralized pricing department that will define, govern, and continuously improve UNFI Canada’s brand and customer pricing strategy. This role will move the organization toward a more disciplined pricing model, shifting pricing ownership away from Sales over time so that Sales can remain focused on customer relationships, execution of brand strategies, and commercial growth. new_jobs.description:
About QuadReal Property Group

QuadReal Property Group is a global real estate investment, development and operating company headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its assets under management are $98.5 billion. From its foundation in Canada as a full-service real estate operating company, QuadReal has expanded its capabilities globally for investments in equity and debt in both the public and private markets. QuadReal invests directly through operating platforms in which it holds an ownership interest and via programmatic partnerships.

QuadReal seeks to deliver strong investment returns while creating sustainable environments that bring value to the people and communities it serves. Now and for generations to come.

QuadReal: Excellence lives here.

www.quadreal.com

Role Description

The Director, Enterprise Data Governance is accountable for defining and governing the enterprise data QuadReal relies on, anchored in DAMA-DMBOK, covering data definitions, ownership, quality, and observability. This makes QuadReal's data reliable enough to be governed, measured, and controlled, reducing the risk that decisions, reporting, and controls rest on data that can't be trusted. The role reports to the VP, Risk & Integrated Assurance and turns the VP's enterprise-wide mandate into one accountable operating model focused on risk mitigation through data governance lens.

Success is measured by the risk it mitigates: data issues caught before they become decisions made on incorrect information, ownership gaps closed before they become accountability gaps. Holding up under audit is one key aspect of that risk mitigation but not the goal in itself.

The Director also supports the VP's overall view of QuadReal's risk and control environment and represents Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Governance
Define QuadReal’s enterprise data definitions, classifications, and Critical Data Elements (CDEs), anchored in DAMA-DMBOK.
Own the data ownership and accountability model: name Data Owners, Stewards, and Custodians, and hold them accountable through a defined sign-off cadence.
Deliver the enterprise business glossary under a tiered governance model, and maintain metadata management, lineage standards, and dbt metadata synchronization across the platform.
Set data quality thresholds and Trusted Layer certification criteria, and hold data observability (freshness, pipeline health, trust scores) to the same standard as financial controls.
Align controls as gates across the data delivery lifecycle (ingestion, definition, build, use, and govern), so a control fires wherever data advances and nothing reaches a certified output without passing.
Build data governance capability across the business through training and playbooks, rather than keeping expertise centralized.
Integration and Decision Authority
Act as the link between Business Controls and Data Governance called for in the integrated operating model: define control standards and evidence expectations alongside data definitions, and build controls into new systems and initiatives from the start.
Where control standards and data definitions conflict, collaborate with relevant stakeholders including, ED&A, Business Owners and Business Controls to resolve these inconsistencies. Work with ED&A / Technology and the Data Platform team so controls and governance are proactively built into the toolchain (Microsoft Fabric, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Purview, Entra ID, Quadrant) by design.
Represent Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance meetings and support Audit Committee reporting.
Team Leadership
Lead and develop direct report(s) and set clear deliverables and cadence for them..
Build team capability in data analytics, AI literacy, and integrated systems controls as the role grows, and build bench strength to move the environment from project to sustained run-state without single points of failure.
Build a “one team” culture between Business Controls and Data Governance that removes duplicate work and closes the gaps that used to sit between the two groups.

What Success Looks Like

Controls operating as gates, each with a named owner and re-performable evidence.
Audit outcomes: clean walkthroughs, deficiencies remediated, and SOC scope defensible.
Glossary and standards adopted, so certified numbers are built on agreed definitions.
Governance measured by delivery: trusted, in-use data products standing behind reported figures.
Direct reports delivering to plan, with growing capability and bench strength.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Risk Management, Data Management, Computer Science, or a related discipline; Master is an asset.
8+ years of progressive experience across data governance, risk management, or audit, including at least 2 years leading people, and demonstrable end-to-end delivery of a control or governance environment.
Working knowledge of ICFR, SOC 1 / ISAE 3402, COSO 2013, ITGCs, and DAMA-DMBOK; CPA, CIA, CISA, or CDMP an asset. Familiarity with DCAM / CDMC and data contracts an asset.
Hands-on experience with data cataloguing and governance tooling (Microsoft Purview equivalents such as Collibra an asset) and with controls testing in an ICFR or SOX environment.
Working knowledge of a modern data-platform stack (Microsoft Fabric / lakehouse, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Entra ID), enough to specify and validate controls.
Working knowledge of Yardi strongly preferred.
Investment and portfolio management literacy or business acumen
Proven ability to build controls that produce retained, re-testable evidence.
Ability to work across Finance, IT, and Data & Analytics, and turn technical and operational complexity into clear governance and control frameworks.
Comfortable preparing materials for senior leadership and the Audit Committee.
Comfortable building or growing an early-stage function.
Experience within real estate, asset management, pension, or investment management environments strongly preferred.

About Us

The Maples Group is a global leader in financial services, trusted by many of the world’s largest hedge fund managers, private equity firms, and international corporations.
Our side-by-side financial and legal teams consistently deliver award-winning services to a global client base, offering unrivalled learning and career opportunities to our 2,500 colleagues worldwide. With 18 locations across the Americas, Asia, Europe and the Middle East, our international presence offers a unique springboard for career development and cross- cultural immersion.

What’s it like to work here?

We are driven to excel, and collaboration is key to our continued success. We can go further for our clients because we go further for each other too. We are committed to diversity, inclusion and equal of opportunity as we attract, retain and develop world-class talent. Our inclusive culture creates an environment where people can be themselves at work while doing their best work. No matter where you work in the Maples Group, you will be part of a global team.

The Opportunity

The Maples Group is seeking a Vice President – Governance & Reporting to join our Internal Audit team in Montreal. This is newly created leadership role is responsible for designing, executing and continuously enhancing the governance, reporting and quality-assurance framework for our global Internal Audit function. Acting as a key architect of our third line of defence, the successful candidate will ensure that Internal Audit delivers clear, timely and data-driven insight to the Audit Committees and key stakeholders, while aligning with the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) global Internal Audit Standards.

Consistently recognised as one of Montreal’s Top Employers, the Maples Group established our operations in the central downtown area in 2009. Our Montreal office exemplifies our culturally rich and entrepreneurial organisation, with over 300 colleagues from 50 countries collaborating to deliver best-in-class solutions to clients worldwide.

Reporting directly to the Senior Vice-President, you will:

Own the end-to-end Internal Audit governance calendar, including timely preparation and delivery of reporting packs for audit meetings
Produce concise, visually engaging dashboards on audit plan delivery, thematic issues, outstanding audit findings, emerging risks and quality metrics for senior stakeholders and the Audit Committees
Design, implement and maintain a comprehensive Quality Assurance and Improvement Programme (QAIP) in line with the IIA Standards and local regulatory requirements
Govern the creation, periodic review and formal approval of audit methodology (IA Charter, Internal Audit Procedures Manual, templates and guidance notes) ensuring timely updates for regulatory and professional-standards changes
Operate the escalation framework for delays, scope changes and impediments, ensuring early and transparent communication
Track and report on audit findings, actions and remediation progress
Manage the automation agenda for Internal Audit, including digitisation of audit processes and report templates, exploration of automation technologies, and enhancement of risk-rating methodologies through data analytics and predictive indicators
Serve as Internal Audit’s primary liaison on governance and quality matters with senior management, risk and compliance heads, and external auditors; present complex technical concepts in a clear, business-oriented manner tailored to diverse audiences

Whilst governance and reporting are the primary functions of this role, the candidate may be requested to assist with or conduct audit engagements.

What You Bring

In addition to indisputably high ethical standards and autonomy, the ideal candidate possesses the following:
A minimum of 5 years’ experience in internal audit within financial services or a similarly regulated environment
Proven expertise in designing and operating an Internal Audit quality-assurance framework; prior responsibility for a QAIP or equivalent is strongly preferred
Strong knowledge of the IIA Standards and associated guidance
Demonstrated success in governance reporting to boards of directors, Audit Committees and regulators, with superior written and verbal communication skills

Key skills and qualifications for this role are as follows:

Attention to detail, professionalism and a team first mentality
Experience with data-analytics and automation tools; ability to translate technology opportunities into practical efficiency gains
Strong understanding of risk and control assessment techniques, risk taxonomies and audit-universe construction
Highly organised self-starter, capable of working independently, managing multiple priorities and influencing without direct authority
Excellent time management, organisational, prioritisation and communication skills (fluent written and oral English)

Benefits & Rewards

The most enduring professional relationships are reciprocal relationships. The Maples Group prioritises employee health and wellbeing. We offer a range of benefits, including:

Comprehensive health coverage (medical, dental and optical)
Competitive vacation packages
Educational assistance and professional development programs
Savings or pension plan
Life insurance
Travel insurance
Global mental wellness program
Social events

“Please note that it is the Maples Group standard policy to undertake various background screening checks on all applicants to whom a conditional job offer is made. Except for roles based in the Republic of Ireland, the background checks will include criminal records checks when a conditional job offer is made. If you have a criminal record, it does not mean that your job offer will be automatically withdrawn. The Maples Group will make all job offer decisions on a case-by-case basis and will take a number of factors into account, such as the role that you are applying for and the nature and circumstances of the past offence. new_jobs.title: Director, Canada Strategy
new_jobs.description:
At Manulife Canada, the Strategy & Transformation team sits at the center of the organization, partnering closely with the Canada CEO and Segment leaders to shape and advance the company’s long-term direction.

We work across business lines and functions to translate Segment strategy into aligned priorities, maintain an integrated view of the strategic portfolio, shape high-impact initiatives, and improve the processes through which strategic and investment decisions are made.

As Director, Canada Strategy, you will help shape Manulife Canada’s strategy and advance its most critical priorities. You will combine enterprise perspective, structured problem solving, and constructive challenge to help senior leaders make clear choices and mobilize action.

This high-visibility role spans strategy reviews, strategic initiatives, and business and functional deep dives. The Director will act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders and help connect Canada Segment priorities with business unit and functional plans.

This role is ideal for a strategy leader who has shaped enterprise or business-unit strategy in a complex organization or top-tier consulting environment and is equally comfortable developing strategy, facilitating executive decisions, and moving priority initiatives toward execution.

Position Responsibilities

Strategy Cascade and Enterprise Visibility

Translate Canada Segment strategy into clear priorities, expectations, and decision criteria for business units and functions.
Lead periodic strategy reviews and structured check-ins to assess progress, test whether priorities remain valid, and identify where leadership intervention is required.
Maintain an integrated view of the strategic portfolio, including both funded initiatives and material work outside the formal book of work, to identify gaps, overlaps, dependencies, and emerging risks.
Synthesize business unit and functional strategies to assess how they collectively advance Canada Segment objectives.
Help develop and communicate the narrative of the Canada Segment strategy to Enterprise leadership and the Board.

Strategic Initiatives and Enterprise Problem Solving

Lead high-priority, cross-business strategic initiatives from problem definition through recommendation, mobilization, and transition to accountable execution owners.
Frame and evaluate strategic choices, including where to enter, exit, invest, partner, acquire, simplify, or double down.
Develop fact-based recommendations through structured problem solving, market and competitive analysis, financial assessment, scenario analysis, and stakeholder input.
Develop business cases and implementation roadmaps, establish intended outcomes and success measures, and secure senior leadership alignment.
Support partnership and M&A assessments, including strategic fit, value creation logic, key risks, and integration considerations, in collaboration with relevant subject-matter experts.

Business and Functional Deep Dives

Lead periodic vertical and horizontal deep dives across businesses and functions, for example – Distribution, Technology, Operations, and other enterprise capabilities.
Act as the Canada Segment’s thought and challenge partner to functions, testing strategic ambition, investment priorities, operating choices, and alignment with business needs.
Identify cross-business opportunities, shared capabilities, and structural barriers that may not be visible within individual portfolios.
Facilitate alignment across business and functional leaders where priorities, accountabilities, or investment choices are unclear.

Executive Advisory and Team Leadership

Provide independent, forward-looking advice to senior executives and facilitate decisions on complex or ambiguous strategic topics.
Develop concise executive and Board-ready materials that clarify the issue, choices, trade-offs, recommendation, and required decision.
Build alignment across business units, functions, and enterprise partners through effective facilitation, influence, and constructive challenge.
Lead and develop a high-performing, inclusive team with strong capabilities in strategic judgment, structured problem solving, executive communication, and delivery.
Coach direct reports and peers, allocate resources to the highest-value priorities
Strengthen the Strategy & Transformation team’s methods and capabilities – including via the adoption of AI, better operating rhythms, common approaches, etc.

Leadership Capabilities

Strategic Judgment: Connect enterprise context, market evidence, economics, and execution realities to make clear recommendations.
Structured Problem Solving: Break ambiguous issues into testable hypotheses, focused analyses, and practical choices.
Influence and Constructive Challenge: Build credibility with senior leaders while testing assumptions and surfacing trade-offs.
Executive Communication: Distill complex issues into concise, decision-oriented narratives and Board-ready materials.
Enterprise Collaboration: Create alignment across business units and functions without relying on formal authority.
Mobilization and Execution: Translate strategy into clear outcomes, accountabilities, success measures, and an executable path forward.
Talent Development: Coach and develop high-performing strategy talent and raise the quality of thinking across the team.

Required Qualifications

8–10+ years of progressively senior experience in corporate strategy, business strategy, management consulting, corporate development, transformation, or a related field.
Experience in financial services and/or a top-tier consulting firm strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience shaping enterprise or business-unit strategy across multiple businesses, functions, or geographies.
Strong financial acumen, including experience developing business cases, assessing investment choices, and evaluating value creation and risk.
Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems, develop and test hypotheses, synthesize quantitative and qualitative evidence, and translate analysis into practical recommendations.
Strong track record of influencing senior stakeholders, facilitating difficult decisions, and delivering measurable outcomes in complex, matrixed environments.
Experience with strategic planning, portfolio prioritization, operating model assessment, transformation, and benefits realization.
People leadership experience, including coaching and developing high-performing teams.
University degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field.
MBA, equivalent graduate degree, or relevant professional designation preferred.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.
